docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who use AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini on a computer where ScienceSoft AI Endpoint Firewall (called AI Firewall in this guide) is installed and managed by their company. If you are trying AI Firewall in a trial, ask your ScienceSoft representative for the trial guide instead.

docs.title: What AI Firewall does
docs.text:
When you send a message, a file or a picture to an AI tool, it can contain private data. This can be a name, a card number, a password or a company secret.

AI Firewall checks your request on your computer, before it leaves. If it finds private data, it follows the rule your company has set. It can record it, replace it with a placeholder, or stop the request.

docs.title: What stays private, and what is recorded
docs.text:
Both are true, so we say both.

  • Stays on your computer: the checking itself. Your messages, files and images are not sent anywhere to be scanned. The private values that were found are not collected.
  • Recorded: if your computer is connected to a workspace, the workspace's administrators can see what was detected: how many values were found and which types. By default the message is also recorded there, with the private values replaced. So they can read what you wrote, but not the personal data found in it. How much is recorded is set by an administrator (the setting is called Data Capture Mode).
  • Whose workspace: normally the workspace belongs to your company. If your computer is connected to a server run by ScienceSoft, as in a trial, ScienceSoft can see what that workspace records.
  • Not connected to a workspace: nothing is sent.

docs.title: Good to know first
docs.text:
• You do not need to do anything every day. AI Firewall works in the background.
  • Your company sets the rules. Many settings are locked. If a rule gets in your way, ask your IT team.
  • It protects only what it covers. An AI tool that is not named on the coverage page is not protected.
  • It must be running. If the app is stopped, protection may stop too, depending on how it was installed. See the coverage page.

docs.text:
Open Help in the app. It has troubleshooting steps and a Contact us form. You can also ask your IT team.

docs.title: Check status
docs.text: This page explains how to check if AI Firewall is protecting you, what each status means, and what to do about it.

docs.title: Where to see the status
docs.text:
• The status card at the bottom of the menu in the app. It shows the status, who sets the rules ("Managed by IT" or "Local settings") and the mode.
  • The Dashboard. The first line shows the same status, in capital letters.
  • The i button at the top right of every screen ("Why this status?"). It lists the checks behind the status and shows which ones passed.

The i window shows three checks:

Check What it means Traffic is steered here Your operating system sends AI-tool traffic to the firewall, so it can be read. Detection engine is at full strength The on-device model that finds sensitive data is running normally. Interception confirmed A test request went through the firewall in the last few minutes.

When all three pass, the window says "Running and protecting: every check passed." If a check fails, it is marked and the status above changes.

Example: the status card when your organisation has paused protection.

docs.title: What each status means
docs.text:
The first rows are the good ones. The later rows need attention.

Status What it means What to do Protecting this device (or Protection is on, when your IT team manages the computer) AI traffic on this computer is checked before it leaves. Nothing. Protected — browsers and proxy-aware apps Browsers and apps that follow the system proxy setting are protected. Other programs are not routed through the firewall at the moment. The screen gives a reason. Nothing you can press. If it stays, tell your IT team. Inspecting with limits Traffic is checked, but one part of detection is not available on this computer (for example the name model, or reading text in images). The screen says which part and what it means. Restart the computer or install a pending update. If it stays, contact your IT team. Mode not confirmed Traffic is checked, but the app could not confirm that the engine is using the mode that was chosen (Record only, Replace or Block). Treat the mode as not applied. See If you see "Mode not confirmed" below. Wait a minute, then restart the app. If it stays, tell your IT team. Checking protection The app is checking. This is normal for a few seconds after start-up. Wait. If it stays for more than a few minutes, the app may be out of date and unable to run the check. It should update itself. If not, contact your IT team. Turning on protection / Turning off protection A change is in progress. Wait. Not inspecting traffic The protection is running, but AI traffic is not reaching it. Nothing is being checked. Open Device & coverage and look at Certificate trust and System proxy to see which part is missing. Tell your IT team. Protection could not start The app could not start protection. The message gives the cause and the fix. Follow the message. If it fails again, contact your IT team. Protection has stopped Protection stopped working. The app is trying to restart it. See When protection has stopped. Wait a moment. If it does not come back, contact your IT team. Protection is paused by your organisation Your IT team paused protection. Only they can turn it back on. See When protection is paused. Contact your IT team if you did not expect this. Some settings remain Protection is off, but some settings could not be removed. AI tools on this computer may not connect. Restart the app. If it stays, contact your IT team. Another AI Firewall app is protecting this computer A second AI Firewall app on this computer checks traffic from desktop apps. Browsers may still be protected by this app. Uninstall one of the two apps, or reinstall this one. Not set up yet This computer is not enrolled. Your IT team needs to finish the setup. Contact your IT team.

docs.title: If you see "Mode not confirmed"
docs.text:
Your AI traffic is still being checked. What is not certain is which mode is in use. Until the status goes back to normal, treat the chosen mode (for example Replace) as not applied: private data might not be replaced or blocked.

The app asks the engine to confirm the mode, and tries three times. The status appears when the engine does not answer in time. Common reasons:

  • The engine restarted, and has not confirmed the mode again yet.
  • The engine was not ready when the mode was set (for example just after start-up or a change of rules).
  • A setting pushed by your IT team did not reach the engine.

What to do:

  1. Wait a minute. When the app sees that the engine is answering again, it sends the mode again by itself.
  2. Restart the app.
  3. If the status stays, tell your IT team. Copy the details from Help (see How to report a problem).

docs.title: When protection has stopped
docs.text:
What happens to your AI requests depends on how AI Firewall was installed.

  • Windows with the system guard, and macOS installed from the .pkg: AI services are blocked on this computer until protection restarts. Nothing is sent without being checked.
  • Any other installation: AI requests still go out, and personal data in them is not checked or replaced. Do not send private data to AI tools until the status is back to "Protecting this device".

In both cases the app is trying to restart the protection by itself.

docs.title: When protection is paused
docs.text:
A pause always comes from your organisation. There is no button for you to turn protection back on.

The title is the same in both cases: Protection is paused by your organisation. The sentence under it tells them apart:

  • "Traffic is still routed through the app, but nothing is being inspected." Nothing is checked, but the connection is not broken.
  • "AI traffic from this device is going out without being inspected." Nothing is routed through the app. AI traffic goes out without being checked.

In both cases, do not send private data to AI tools until your IT team turns protection back on.

docs.title: How to report a problem
docs.text:
1. Open Help and select Copy details.
  2. Select Contact us, describe the problem and paste the details. Personal data in the message is replaced before it is sent, and you see what will be sent.
  3. Or send the details to your IT team.

docs.title: What is protected
docs.text: This page explains what AI Firewall protects, what it does when it finds private data, and what it does not cover.

docs.title: What AI Firewall looks for
docs.text:
AI Firewall reads your request on your computer, before it goes to the AI tool. It can find 32 kinds of private data. 20 of them are on by default. Examples:

  • names and contact details
  • ID numbers and bank card numbers
  • passwords and secret keys
  • other personal or confidential details

The Protection screen shows the full list, in four groups: People, Credentials, Financial and Government identity.

It also checks:

  • Files: Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF.
  • Images and screenshots: it reads the text inside the picture.

docs.title: What it does when it finds something
docs.text:
There are three choices. Each one is a mode.

Mode (top bar) Name on the Protection screen What happens When it fits Monitor Record only The request is sent as you typed it, and a log entry shows what left your computer. The one exception is machine secrets such as API keys: those are replaced by default. The first days, to see what is really being sent. This is the default for new teams. Mask Replace (recommended) Private details are swapped for placeholders before sending. They are put back in the answer you read. The AI can still help you. A detection is replaced only when the firewall is sure enough (see below). Everyday use. Protect Block A request is not sent when the firewall is sure enough (see below) that it holds private data. You see what was found. You can edit your prompt and try again. When private data must never leave your computer.

How sure is "sure enough"? Each finding has a confidence score, and two checks use it differently:

  • Names, organisations and addresses (found by the language model). A finding below the model's cutoff is dropped: it is not replaced and it is not recorded as a detection. The cutoff is set for each kind of finding. The model ScienceSoft ships is tuned to lean towards catching names, so a name it is only fairly sure about is still replaced. Your IT team can change the cutoff for each kind.
  • Numbers and codes found by patterns (cards, account numbers, ID numbers, e-mail addresses). In Replace and Block a weak match, for example an ordinary word that looks like a bank code, is not replaced and does not block a request. It stays in the record of what was found, and the log on this computer shows it. In Record only every match is recorded.

You cannot change this on your computer. Ask your IT team what is set.

Detection of passwords and other credentials is always on. It cannot be switched off. What happens to a credential still depends on the mode: it is blocked in Block mode, replaced in Replace mode, and recorded in Record only mode (except machine secrets, which are replaced).

Because Monitor is the default, a new team is not yet replacing most private data. Ask your IT team which mode is set for you.

docs.title: Who chooses the mode
docs.text:
Your company decides. Your IT team sets the rules for all computers. You cannot change the mode or the list of data types in the app. The Protection screen shows them, so you know what protects you, and shows how long ago your rules were last updated. If the computer is not connected to a company, the app uses the default: Record only.

What you can change on your own computer:

  • Company patterns: your own patterns for things only your company would recognise. They stay on your computer.
  • The detection model and the languages for reading text in images (Detection engine screen).
  • Notifications, and whether AI Firewall starts with your computer.
  • Command-line tools: whether Claude Code, Codex or Kimi Code go through the firewall (see below).

docs.title: Where it works
docs.text:
Where you use AI Covered? Web browsers: Chrome, Edge, Safari Yes, automatically Firefox Yes, if it is set to "Use system proxy settings" Desktop apps built on web technology, such as Claude Desktop Yes, automatically Claude Code Yes, after it is turned on Codex Yes, after it is turned on Kimi Code Yes, after it is turned on

You do not need to set anything up for Claude Desktop. It is covered automatically.

Command-line tools are off until someone turns them on. These tools do not follow the system proxy setting, so AI Firewall has to change each tool's own settings. It does not do that unless you ask, or your IT team asks. Until then, the tool's requests are not checked.

  • To turn a tool on yourself, open Device & coverage and select Connect a command-line tool.
  • Your IT team can also turn tools on for the whole company.
  • Turning protection off, or uninstalling, puts the tool's settings back.
  • Start a new session of the tool afterwards. A session that was already running keeps its old settings.
  • Claude Code and Kimi Code cannot both be covered at once.
  • On Device & coverage, the row Command-line tools shows if they are covered.

At the time of writing, AI Firewall covers 38 AI services in the browser, including Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Perplexity and Grok. The list grows with new versions.

docs.title: What is checked inside a request
docs.text:
• What you type, and what your AI tools read back (for example, files that Claude Code reads for you).
  • Images and screenshots (text is read on your computer).
  • Documents: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF and OpenDocument files, and .zip files one level deep. In Replace mode, a cleaned copy is sent instead of the original.
  • A file that cannot be read (encrypted, damaged, unknown format, or a zip inside a zip) is recorded as not checked, with the reason. By default it is still sent. Your IT team can choose to refuse such files instead.

docs.title: What is NOT covered
docs.text:
We state this clearly, so you never find out by accident.

  • Command-line tools that are not turned on, and all other command-line tools, including curl and your own scripts. They send requests straight to AI services.
  • Aider, Visual Studio Code, Cursor and Continue. AI Firewall does not set these up. Cursor's built-in browser side is covered like any web-based app.
  • JetBrains AI Assistant. Not covered today.
  • Documents attached in Microsoft 365 Copilot. They are stored in your company's OneDrive and read there, so they never pass through the firewall. They are not checked. Each upload is recorded as "An attachment's contents were not inspected". Images attached in Copilot are checked. Your IT team can choose to block these uploads.
  • Apps that pin their own certificate. AI Firewall cannot read their traffic, and the connection fails instead of being skipped.
  • Some VPN clients. A VPN can take over the network setting. When that happens, the agent records it and your IT team can see it.
  • Anything encrypted by the app itself before it reaches the network.
  • Any AI service not named in the list. There is no catch-all.

An AI tool that is not named in this guide is not protected.

docs.title: Known side effect: Microsoft Teams and Outlook
docs.text: To cover Microsoft 365 Copilot, AI Firewall also inspects graph.microsoft.com. The Teams, Outlook and Office desktop apps pin their certificate for this address. On a computer that has them, they may fail to sign in or send messages while protection is on. If that happens, tell your IT team. Turning protection off restores them.

docs.title: When AI Firewall is not running
docs.text:
The app can be closed, for example with Quit in the tray menu. When it is closed, protection stops.

  • Windows with the system guard, and macOS installed from the .pkg: AI services it covers become unavailable instead of being reached without protection. Your IT team can grant an exception. On macOS this holds for the network connections the Mac had at install time. A connection added later, such as a USB adapter, can reach AI services directly.
  • macOS installed from the .dmg: there is no system guard. If the app is closed, AI services are reached directly and your requests are not protected.

The app says so on its own screen, and the device reports it to your IT team.

docs.title: Languages and limits
docs.text:
• Languages: the detection model, the ScienceSoft PII Encoder, supports 7 languages: English, Russian, Arabic, Spanish, German, Italian and French. Images in these languages are read on your computer.
  • Images: the app reads one language group at a time (Latin, Cyrillic or Arabic letters). A picture in a different language may be read badly, without a warning. Reading text from blurry or low-quality images is less accurate.
  • Arabic person names are not found yet.

docs.title: What is recorded
docs.text:
Protection happens on your computer. The private values that were found are not collected.

If your computer is connected to a workspace, the workspace's administrators can see what was detected: how many values were found and which types. By default the message is also recorded there, with the private values replaced. So they can read what you wrote, but not the personal data found in it.

How much is recorded is set by an administrator. The setting is called Data Capture Mode (TraceContent). It has three levels:

Level What the workspace keeps Full (the default) The conversation, with the private values replaced. Masked A short excerpt of the text with the private values replaced, with the detection record. Metadata Only what was detected. No message text.

Whose workspace it is matters. Normally it belongs to your company. If your computer is connected to a server run by ScienceSoft, as in a trial, ScienceSoft can see what that workspace records. ScienceSoft can disconnect a computer on request.

A computer that is not connected to a workspace sends nothing.

What the AI service receives depends on the mode (see the table above).

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Short answers to the questions people ask most. For steps to fix a problem, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Can my manager read my chats?
docs.text:
This tool has two jobs: it keeps your company's confidential data out of the prompts that your apps send to AI services, and it collects as little as possible about you while doing that.

Plainly:

  • The workspace's administrators can see what was detected: how many values were found, and which types. They cannot see the values themselves.
  • If your computer is connected to a workspace, the message is also recorded there, by default, with those values replaced. So they can read what you wrote, but not the personal data that was found in it. An administrator can choose to keep less (a short excerpt, or no message text at all). The setting is called Data Capture Mode.
  • What the AI service receives depends on your company's setting. In Replace mode, values that the firewall is sure enough about are replaced before sending. In Record only mode, your message is sent as typed, apart from machine secrets such as API keys.
  • A computer that is not connected to a workspace sends nothing.

docs.title: Is my data sent anywhere to be scanned?
docs.text: No. Your messages, files and images are checked on your computer. The detection model runs on your computer too.

docs.title: Does AI Firewall read all my internet traffic?
docs.text: No. Only traffic to AI services is sent through it. Every other site goes straight out, untouched and unread.

docs.title: Does ScienceSoft see my data?
docs.text:
Only if your computer is connected to a server run by ScienceSoft, as in a trial. Then ScienceSoft can see what that workspace records. ScienceSoft can disconnect a computer from its server on request.

In a normal installation, the workspace belongs to your company, and ScienceSoft does not see it.

docs.title: Why does it install a certificate? Is that safe?
docs.text:
AI traffic is encrypted. To check a request before it leaves, your computer has to trust AI Firewall. The certificate does that.

  • It is made on your computer.
  • It works on this computer only.
  • Its private key never leaves your computer.

docs.title: Do I need to do anything every day?
docs.text: No. AI Firewall works in the background. Open the app when you want to see what it did, or when something looks wrong.

docs.title: Can I turn protection off?
docs.text:
No. There is no on/off switch in the app. Your company decides when protection is on.

You can close the app from the tray menu, but then nothing is checked. Depending on how AI Firewall was installed, AI services are then either blocked or reached without being checked (see What is protected). Your IT team can see that the device has stopped reporting.

docs.title: Does it slow down my AI tools?
docs.text: A little. The Dashboard shows the median scan time measured on your own computer. Large screenshots take longer, because the text inside them is read first.

docs.title: Why was a name replaced when it was my own?
docs.text: The detection model does not know which names are safe in your work. Tell your IT team, and they can add an exception for your team. You cannot add one yourself.

docs.title: What happens if AI Firewall stops working?
docs.text:
It says so, and does not pretend otherwise. The status changes (see Check status), and Device & coverage stops showing the affected traffic as covered.

What happens to your AI requests depends on how AI Firewall was installed:

  • On Windows with the system guard, and on macOS installed from the .pkg, AI services are blocked until protection is back.
  • In other installations, requests go out without being checked. Do not send private data until the status is back to "Protecting this device".

docs.title: Does it work with Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini?
docs.text: Yes, in your browser and in desktop apps built on web technology (for example Claude Desktop). Claude Code, Codex and Kimi Code are covered too, after they are turned on (see What is protected). The full list, and what is not covered, is on the same page.

docs.title: What does it do with files and images?
docs.text:
Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF and OpenDocument files are opened on your computer and their text is checked. For images and screenshots, the text inside the picture is read on your computer. In Replace mode, a cleaned copy of a file is sent instead of the original.

A file that cannot be read (for example an encrypted file) is recorded as not checked. By default it is still sent. Your IT team can choose to refuse such files instead.

docs.title: Which languages does it support?
docs.text: The detection model, the ScienceSoft PII Encoder, supports 7 languages: English, Russian, Arabic, Spanish, German, Italian and French. Arabic person names are not detected yet (see What is protected).

docs.title: What is not protected?
docs.text: An AI tool that is not named on What is protected is not protected. Examples: other command-line tools, scripts, and the JetBrains AI Assistant.

docs.title: Does the app update itself?
docs.text: Yes, or your IT team delivers updates, if they manage them. Every update must be signed by ScienceSoft and newer than the version you have, and the app never asks you for a password. When an update is ready, select Restart now. The restart takes a few seconds, and AI traffic pauses briefly.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: This page explains how AI Firewall gets onto your computer and how to check that it works.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A Windows or macOS computer. There is no Linux version.
  • Permission to approve a security certificate on this computer. On Windows this needs an administrator account. On macOS you need your login password.
  • An internet connection.

docs.title: Two ways to install
docs.text:
Your company chooses one of these.

Way 1: You install it Way 2: Your IT team installs it Who does the work You Your IT team, on many computers at once What you receive An installer file from your IT team (.exe on Windows, .dmg on macOS) Nothing. The app just appears. What you do Follow the steps below Approve the certificate if asked, then check that it works (Steps 3 and 4)

docs.title: Step 1. Run the installer
docs.text:
1. Open the installer file you received.
  2. Follow the on-screen steps and finish the installation.
  3. Open AI Firewall.

docs.title: Step 2. Connect to your company
docs.text:
The enrollment code is the key that joins this computer to your company's workspace. You do not type it in the app. It is given to the installer as an argument when the installer is run. Your IT team does this: they either run the installer for you, or give you the command to run. The switches are described in Roll out the agent.

Treat the enrollment code like a password. Do not paste it into chats, tickets or AI tools.

Trial only

In a trial, the app asks for a server address and an enrollment code from your welcome email. Your ScienceSoft representative can send you the trial guide.

docs.title: Step 3. Approve the certificate
docs.text:
AI traffic is encrypted. To read a request before it leaves your computer, AI Firewall needs your computer to trust it. It does this with a certificate.

  1. A prompt appears. On Windows it is a security prompt. On macOS it asks for your login password.
  2. Read it. The certificate is issued to AI Firewall.
  3. Approve it.

About this certificate:

  • It is made on your computer and works on this computer only.
  • Its private key never leaves your computer.
  • If you decline, AI Firewall cannot read encrypted traffic. It will tell you this. It will not pretend that you are protected.

[screenshot: certificate prompt]

docs.title: Step 4. Check that it works
docs.text:
1. Open Device & coverage in the app.
  2. Find Certificate trust. It must say Yes — installed.

If it says anything else, see If something goes wrong below.

docs.title: Way 2: Your IT team installs it
docs.text:
Your IT team installs AI Firewall for the whole company. You do not need to download or set up anything.

You may still see the certificate prompt described in Step 3. Approve it. Then check that it works with Step 4.

Your IT team can find the deployment details in Roll out the agent.

docs.title: What your company can see
docs.text:
AI Firewall works on your computer. The text you type, your files and your images are checked on your computer. They are not sent anywhere to be scanned.

If your computer is connected to a workspace, the workspace's administrators can see what was detected (how many values and which types) and what was done about it. By default the message is also recorded there, with the private values already replaced. So they can read what you wrote, but not the personal data found in it. An administrator can choose to keep less (the setting is called Data Capture Mode).

The private values themselves are not collected. A computer that is not connected to a workspace sends nothing.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
What you see What to do Certificate trust is not Yes — installed You may have declined the prompt. A banner at the top of the app offers Install certificate. Select it and approve the prompt this time. The app says the code was not accepted Check that you copied the whole code. If it still fails, ask your IT team for a new one. The app says it cannot reach the server Check your internet connection. A company network or VPN may block the request. Ask your IT team.

If AI Firewall is closed or stopped, AI services are either unavailable or reached without protection, depending on how it was installed. See When AI Firewall is not running. Start the app again.

For more problems, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Using the app
docs.text:
This page explains the AI Firewall app: what each screen shows and what you can do on it.

AI Firewall protects you in the background. You do not need to open the app for it to work. Open it when you want to see what it did, or when something looks wrong.

docs.title: The app at a glance
docs.text:
The app has a menu on the left. It has three groups.

Group Screen What it is for Monitor Dashboard Today's summary: is protection running, and what did it do? Monitor Activity Every request the firewall saw, and what it did with each one. Configure Protection What the firewall looks for, and what happens when it finds something. Configure AI tools protection The skills and MCP servers installed on this computer. Configure Detection engine The on-device model that finds sensitive data. This device Device & coverage Connection to your company, and which AI traffic is covered. This device Updates The installed version and how updates arrive. This device Help Troubleshooting, common questions and who to ask.

At the bottom of the menu, a status card shows if protection is on, for example "Protection is on". It also shows who sets the rules ("Managed by IT" or "Local settings") and the mode. Below it you see the app version and a button to switch between light and dark theme. The button at the top of the menu folds it to icons.

There is no on/off switch in the app. Your company decides when protection is on. You can close the app from the tray menu (Quit), but then protection stops. See When AI Firewall is not running.

The i button at the top of every screen ("Why this status?") shows the checks behind the current status. For the meaning of each status, see Check status.

docs.title: Who is in charge: you or your IT team
docs.text:
Your IT team sets the rules. You cannot change the mode or the list of data types in the app. You can see them, so you know what protects you. Where a rule is set by your IT team, the screen says "Set by your IT team. To change it, contact them."

Things you can change on your own computer:

  • Company patterns (Protection screen).
  • Detection model and the languages for reading text in images (Detection engine screen).
  • Notifications, Start with this laptop, and saving, restoring or resetting your settings (Device & coverage screen).
  • Command-line tools: which tools go through the firewall (Device & coverage screen).

Restoring or resetting your settings never changes the rules set by your IT team.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
Shows today's picture:

  • A headline, for example "No AI traffic was inspected on this laptop today."
  • A bar showing how requests were handled, and tiles such as most common find, busiest AI tool and number of AI tools inspected.
  • Traffic by AI tool: which AI tools were used today.
  • What was protected: what kinds of data were found. "Adjust" opens the Protection screen.

Two buttons take you on: Review today's activity and See what is protected.

If the lists are empty, nothing has been scanned yet. Requests to AI services will appear as you use them.

docs.title: Activity
docs.text:
[screenshot: Activity, the Requests tab]

Everything stays on your computer. There are three tabs.

  • Apps: which apps talked to which AI services. Open a row to see details.
  • Requests: every request, newest first, with time, size and scan time. Open a row to see what was found and what was done.
  • Conversations: the same traffic shown as chats. You can search messages, tools and chats, and filter by who sent the message or by tool.

If the list is empty, the screen tells you why. For example, protection may be paused, or AI traffic is not reaching the firewall yet. In that case open Device & coverage to see which part is missing.

docs.title: Protection
docs.text:
This screen shows what is protecting you. The mode and the data types are read-only. You can look, but not change them.

When sensitive data is found in a request. Three modes:

Name What happens Record only The request is sent as typed. You get a log entry so you know what left your computer. Replace Details are swapped for placeholders, then put back in the answer you read. Block The request is not sent. You see what was found and can edit the prompt and try again.

Details of what each mode does, including the exceptions for machine secrets, are on the page What is protected.

What the firewall looks for. 32 types of data in four groups: People, Credentials, Financial and Government identity. The heading shows how many are on, for example "10 of 32 types active". Each type shows how many were found today. A type marked "Not detected yet" cannot be found by the firewall at the moment. Credential detection is always on.

A type that is switched off is not replaced, but the firewall still records that it saw it, so your IT team can spot a gap.

AI services this applies to. The AI services that are inspected. A service that is not on the list is not inspected.

Things only your company would recognise. Patterns specific to your company, for example an internal project code. You can add your own with Add a company pattern, and remove them again. They stay on your computer. Patterns pushed by your IT team are separate and read-only.

Never replace these. A list of terms that are never replaced. It is set by your IT team and you cannot change it. If something is replaced that should not be, tell your IT team.

docs.title: AI tools protection
docs.text:
[screenshot: AI tools protection, with neutral example tools]

Lists the skills and MCP servers found in the configuration files on your computer. Nothing is sent while it looks.

  • A skill is a set of instructions the AI model follows. An MCP server is a program the AI tool can call.
  • Scan now looks again.
  • For each item you see its name, type (MCP server or skill), the tool it belongs to, where it is configured, and a risk level (high, medium, low) with the reason.
  • "Could not be read" means a configuration file could not be parsed.

This is a list, not an approval. Nobody has reviewed these items, and an MCP server that opens its own connection is not inspected by the firewall.

docs.title: Detection engine
docs.text:
Shows how the firewall finds data. Two things run on every request: pattern matching (always on) and a language model that finds names, addresses and similar free text.

  • Model in use: the models you can choose from, with size, languages and download state. You can choose a model on your own computer.
  • Text inside images: the languages used to read text in pictures. You can add or remove a language.

These choices are local to your computer. Your IT team does not lock them.

docs.title: Device & coverage
docs.text:
Shows the state of this computer.

This device: status, your company's server, enrolment state, when the app last checked in, device ID, policy version, app version, and whether the certificate is trusted ("Yes — installed"). If the connection to your company's server fails, the screen explains why and offers Try connecting again. Protection keeps running either way. The connection only affects settings and reports.

Coverage: which AI traffic passes through the firewall.

  • Browsers and desktop apps
  • Command-line tools (Claude Code, Codex and Kimi Code)
  • Tools that those tools start

Each one is shown as Covered, Partial or Not covered, with a reason.

AI services covered: the services and addresses that are inspected.

Install certificate. If the certificate is missing, a banner appears at the top: AI Firewall needs to install a security certificate to inspect AI traffic. Select Install certificate and approve the prompt.

Connect a command-line tool. Claude Code, Codex and Kimi Code do not follow the system proxy, so they are off until you turn them on. Select this button, choose the tool, and follow the three steps. AI Firewall then changes that tool's own settings so its requests go through the firewall. Turning protection off, or uninstalling, puts the settings back. Start a new session of the tool afterwards. Your IT team can also turn tools on for the whole company.

What you are told about. Choose which notifications you get. Some are always on and cannot be turned off, for example "A request was not sent" and "Protection stopped".

This laptop. Start with this laptop, save a copy of your settings, restore from a copy, or reset to defaults.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
Shows the installed version, the newest version and when the app last checked.

  • Check now looks for an update.
  • Restart now appears when an update is ready. The restart takes a few seconds, and AI traffic pauses briefly.
  • Every update is checked before it is installed: it must be signed by ScienceSoft and newer than the current version. The app never asks you for a password.
  • If your IT team manages updates, the screen says so. You stay protected on the installed version until they deliver the update.
  • If the app cannot update itself on your computer, an orange banner says so and asks you to contact your IT administrator.

docs.title: Help and Contact us
docs.text:
Help has troubleshooting steps and common questions, including:

  • Protection is on but nothing appears in Activity
  • Names are not replaced, but emails and card numbers are
  • Something was replaced that should not have been
  • My command-line tool is not being inspected
  • A setting will not change
  • What happens if the firewall stops working?

It also has Copy details, to send technical details to support, and Contact us.

Contact us: choose Ask a question, Report a problem or Request a call, and write a message. The message is checked on your computer first. Personal data is replaced before it is sent, and you see exactly what will be sent before you press Send this. It needs a connection to your company's workspace.

Remove this app is on the Help screen on macOS. On Windows, remove it in Settings > Apps. See Uninstall.

docs.title: Messages you may see
docs.text:
For the protection status, see Check status. These are other messages.

Message What it means Reduced detection on this laptop Protection is on, but part of detection is not running (for example name detection). Restart the computer or install a pending update. If it stays, contact your IT team. Audit log upload Reports to your company's server are failing. Protection keeps working, and records wait on your computer until the problem is fixed. Connections to AI services The firewall could not connect to an AI service. The message says what failed and who can fix it. Downloading protection… The detection model is downloading. Update needs attention The last update did not finish, or the app cannot update itself on this computer. Select Retry now or Check now, or contact your IT administrator.

docs.title: Trial only
docs.text: In a trial build, the app asks for a server address and an enrollment code from your welcome email. It shows a notice when the trial is about to end, and says that when it ends the device stops reporting to the workspace, while protection on the computer continues. Your ScienceSoft representative can send you the trial guide.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page helps you when AI Firewall does not behave as you expect. Find your problem in the list, then follow the steps. If a status in the app is not green, read Check status first.

docs.title: Quick list
docs.text: Problem Go to The status is not "Protecting this device" Check status Protection is on, but Activity is empty Problem 1 Names are not replaced, or nothing is replaced at all Problem 2 Something of mine was replaced that should not have been Problem 3 My command-line tool is not checked Problem 4 A setting will not change Problem 5 Certificate trust is not "Yes — installed" Problem 6 The app cannot reach your company's server Problem 7 Teams or Outlook cannot sign in Problem 8 AI tools stopped working when I closed the app Problem 9 AI tools feel slower Problem 10

docs.title: Problem 1. Protection is on, but Activity is empty
docs.text:
Activity only fills after you send something to an AI service from this computer.

  1. Use an AI tool (for example, send a short message in a browser).
  2. Open Activity again.
  3. If it is still empty, open Device & coverage. Look at Browsers and desktop apps.
  4. If it is not Covered, the certificate or the system proxy is not in place. Your AI traffic is going out directly, without being checked. Look at Certificate trust and System proxy on the same screen to see which part is missing. Then see Problem 6, or contact your IT team.

The empty Activity screen also gives a reason, for example "Protection is paused" or "Nothing is reaching the firewall yet".

If you only use Claude Code, Codex or Kimi Code, see Problem 4: they are off until they are turned on.

docs.title: Problem 2. Names are not replaced, or nothing is replaced
docs.text:
There are two different causes. Check the first one first.

  1. The mode. Open Protection. If the mode is Record only, the request is sent as you typed it. Only machine secrets, such as API keys, are replaced. This is the default for new teams. Ask your IT team if this is what they want.
  2. The detection model. Emails and card numbers are found by patterns, which always run. Names are found by a language model. If it is still downloading, or could not start, names are not replaced. Open Detection engine to see which model is in use and whether it started. A notice "Downloading protection…" means the download is still going.

Arabic names are not detected yet.

docs.title: Problem 3. Something was replaced that should not have been
docs.text:
The detection model does not know which names or words are safe in your work.

Tell your IT team the exact word and what it was replaced with. They can add an exception for your team. You cannot add exceptions yourself: the list of words that are never replaced is set by your IT team.

docs.title: Problem 4. My command-line tool is not checked
docs.text:
Command-line tools do not follow the system proxy setting. They are off until someone turns them on. Until then, their requests are not checked.

  1. Open Device & coverage. Look at Command-line tools. It must say Covered.
  2. If it does not, select Connect a command-line tool, choose Claude Code, Codex or Kimi Code, and follow the steps. Your IT team can also turn tools on for the whole company.
  3. Start a new session of the tool. A session that was already running keeps its old settings.
  4. Claude Code and Kimi Code cannot both be covered at once.
  5. Any other command-line tool is not covered. See What is protected.

docs.title: Problem 5. A setting will not change
docs.text:
If your IT team manages your computer, they set the rules. The mode and the list of data types are always read-only in the app. A banner says "Managed by your IT team" on the screens where your IT team sets a rule. To change a rule, contact them.

You can change company patterns, the detection model, image languages, notifications and the start-up setting yourself.

docs.title: Problem 6. Certificate trust is not "Yes — installed"
docs.text:
Without the certificate, AI Firewall cannot read encrypted AI traffic.

  1. A banner at the top of the app says AI Firewall needs to install a security certificate. Select Install certificate.
  2. Approve the prompt from your operating system. On Windows it needs an administrator account. On macOS it asks for your login password.
  3. Open Device & coverage. Certificate trust must now say Yes — installed.

If you declined the prompt, repeat the steps and approve it this time. More details are on Install.

docs.title: Problem 7. The app cannot reach your company's server
docs.text:
Protection on your computer keeps running. The connection only affects settings and reports.

Open Device & coverage. The line Why explains what happened.

What the screen says What it means and what to do The server rejected this device's credentials, or does not recognise this device any more The enrolment was probably reset or removed. Contact your IT team: the device needs to be enrolled again. This device can't reach the server Check your network, VPN or firewall. This usually clears on its own. The server is returning errors Usually temporary. Wait, then try again.

Select Try connecting again to ask the server to accept this device again.

docs.title: Problem 8. Teams or Outlook cannot sign in
docs.text: To cover Microsoft 365 Copilot, AI Firewall also checks graph.microsoft.com. The Teams, Outlook and Office desktop apps pin their certificate for that address, so they may fail to sign in or send messages while protection is on. Tell your IT team. Turning protection off restores them, but only your IT team can do that.

docs.title: Problem 9. AI tools stopped working when I closed the app
docs.text:
On Windows with the system guard, and on macOS installed from the .pkg, the AI services that AI Firewall covers are blocked while the app is not running. This protects you: requests are not sent unchecked. Start the app again. Your IT team can grant an exception.

On macOS installed from the .dmg, nothing is blocked. If the app is closed, AI requests go out without being checked.

docs.title: Problem 10. AI tools feel slower
docs.text: A little delay is normal. Dashboard shows the median scan time measured on your own computer. Large screenshots take longer, because the text inside them is read first. If the delay is large, contact your IT team.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text:
1. Open Help and select Copy details.
  2. Select Contact us, choose Report a problem, and write what happened. Paste the details.
  3. Your message is checked on your computer first. Personal data is replaced before it is sent, and you see what will be sent.
  4. Or send the details to your IT team.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: This page explains how to remove AI Firewall from your computer, and what happens when you do.

docs.title: Read this first
docs.text:
• You need administrator access. AI Firewall runs as a protected part of the system. A standard user cannot stop or remove it. This is on purpose: it keeps protection from being switched off by mistake. If you do not have administrator rights, ask your IT team.
  • Your company may not allow it. If your IT team manages your computer, they decide whether AI Firewall stays. Please ask them before you remove it.
  • After removal you are not protected. Requests to AI tools are no longer checked.
  • An update is not an uninstall. Updates keep your data and your connection to your company. Only an uninstall removes them.
  • Quit the app first. Quit AI Firewall from the tray menu before you uninstall, so it puts the settings of your command-line tools back.

AI Firewall is available for Windows and macOS. There is no Linux version.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
1. Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps.
  2. Find AI Firewall followed by the version number, for example AI Firewall 2.2.7.
  3. Select the three-dot menu, then Uninstall. (Modify is greyed out. You cannot change the installation.)
  4. Approve the administrator prompt (UAC).

AI Firewall is installed for every user of the computer, so removing it needs an administrator. If you are signed in as a standard user, Windows asks for the name and password of an administrator. Without them nothing is removed. If you do not have them, ask your IT team.

docs.title: What the uninstaller removes
docs.text:
• The app and its folder in C:\Program Files\AI Firewall.
  • The protection services and scheduled tasks that restart the app.
  • The system proxy setting that sends AI traffic through the firewall. Your browsers go back to normal. If a browser is already open, restart it.
  • The AI Firewall certificate ("AI Firewall Local CA"), from the computer and from every user.
  • The browser settings that AI Firewall added.
  • The settings AI Firewall added for Claude Code and Codex. Your own settings are kept. If Claude Code pointed at the firewall, its original address is put back.
  • Your local data, for every user on the computer: the activity history, saved settings, logs and the connection to your company.

docs.title: Silent uninstall, for IT teams
docs.text: IT teams can remove AI Firewall without prompts. See Windows and macOS in the Admin Guide.

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
Do not drag the app to the Trash. That removes only the app. The certificate, the proxy setting and the background services stay on the computer.

Use the uninstall script that comes with the app. It works for every kind of installation (.dmg and .pkg).

  1. Quit AI Firewall from the menu bar.
  2. Open Finder > Applications.
  3. Right-click AI Firewall and select Show Package Contents.
  4. Open Contents/Resources.
  5. Double-click uninstall.command.
  6. When asked, type remove and press Enter.
  7. Enter your administrator password when asked.

Or, from Terminal:

"/Applications/AI Firewall.app/Contents/Resources/uninstall.command"

[screenshot: the uninstall script asking for confirmation]

docs.title: What the script removes
docs.text:
• The app, and its settings, preferences and logs.
  • The background services and the login item.
  • The AI Firewall certificate, from the login keychain and the System keychain.
  • The system proxy setting, on every network connection, if it points at AI Firewall.
  • The settings that AI Firewall added for Claude Code and Codex at the system level.
  • Your local data and the connection to your company.

The script removes data only for the user who runs it. Another user on the same Mac keeps their local data.

docs.title: If something is left behind on macOS
docs.text:
The script says on screen what it did and what it left. Read its last lines.

  • The proxy setting. The script switches off the automatic proxy setting on every network connection that points at AI Firewall. A connection whose setting it cannot confirm as its own, for example your company's own proxy, it leaves alone, and says so in a line that starts with "Left the auto-proxy". If AI sites do not load afterwards, open System Settings > Network, select your connection, open Details > Proxies, and switch off Automatic proxy configuration.
  • Your own Claude Code settings. The script removes the settings that AI Firewall added for Claude Code at the system level. It does not edit your own Claude Code settings file. If Claude Code still points at the firewall, remove the address that points at 127.0.0.1 from your Claude Code settings.

docs.title: What happens to your data
docs.text:
• On your computer: the activity history is deleted, and so is the list of replaced values. Once it is gone, replaced values cannot be turned back into the original text. The connection to your company is deleted too. If you install AI Firewall again, it is a fresh start.
  • At your company: depending on the version, the app may send a short notice to your company's server when you uninstall. The device then shows as removed in the admin console. If no notice is sent, the device simply stops reporting.
  • The device record and the history of what was recorded stay on the server. Your administrator removes the device's access and frees the licence seat. Uninstalling does not delete anything at your company.
  • No notice is sent when your IT team removes the app for many computers at once.

docs.title: After uninstalling: check
docs.text:
• Your browser opens AI sites normally. If a site does not load, restart the browser.
  • The AI Firewall icon is gone from the menu bar or the tray.

docs.title: Things that may stay behind
docs.text:
• An empty C:\Program Files\AI Firewall folder on Windows.
  • Settings for other tools that AI Firewall did not add. AI Firewall does not set up Aider, Continue, Cursor or Visual Studio Code, so there is nothing to remove. AI Firewall does not write to the Claude Code instructions file (CLAUDE.md), so there is no note of ours to remove there.
  • On macOS, other users' local data (see above).

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Can I remove it to reinstall a newer version? You do not need to. Install the new version over the old one. Your data and your connection to your company stay.

I want to reconnect to a different company workspace. Uninstall, then install again. The connection to the old workspace is removed on purpose, so a new install does not join it again by itself.

Does uninstalling delete what my company has recorded about me? No. Those records stay on your company's server.

docs.title: Admin Guide
docs.text:
This guide is for the IT or platform team that sets up ScienceSoft AI Endpoint Firewall (called AI Firewall in this guide) in an organisation.

AI Firewall has two parts:

Part What it is Who uses it The server (control plane) A self-hosted service where your security team sets policy, watches how AI tools are used and reviews audit records. It runs on one Linux server that you own. IT and security administrators The agent A small program on each employee's computer. It checks requests to AI tools and applies the policy. Installed on every managed computer

All data stays in your environment. The server is installed and run by you.

docs.title: What this guide covers
docs.text: Page Read it to learn Prerequisites What you need before you start: the server, the network, and what you receive from us. Install the server Step by step: from an empty Ubuntu server to a working AI Firewall. The installer script Download install.sh with its README and checksum, and how to use it. aifw commands Every aifw command with example output: setup, status, doctor, backup, upgrade. Reverse proxy How to put your own load balancer or proxy in front of the server. Sign-in and roles The first sign-in, who can do what, and the sign-in service console. Single sign-on Letting people sign in with your company directory, for example Microsoft Entra ID. Operate and upgrade Checking health, upgrades and rolling back. Backup and restore What to back up, how, and how to bring the server back. Troubleshooting What to do when the installation or sign-in does not work. Roll out the agent Installing the agent on many Windows and macOS computers, and checking that they joined.

docs.title: The installation at a glance
docs.text:
1. Get the server ready and the network open (see Prerequisites).
  2. Run the installer script install.sh. It installs Docker and the aifw command.
  3. Run aifw preflight, then aifw setup. Setup asks a few questions and does the rest.
  4. Save the sign-in details that setup shows, then sign in to the admin portal.

It takes about 20 minutes on a prepared server.

If you have questions that this guide does not answer, contact your ScienceSoft representative.

docs.title: aifw command reference
docs.text:
aifw installs and operates the whole server. It is the only supported way to install the server. The sequence is:

sudo bash install.sh     # installs the aifw command (see "The installer script")
sudo aifw setup          # installs and configures the server

Find your command in the summary table, then read its section. Every command is run with sudo.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Access: SSH to the server, and an account that can use sudo.
  • The aifw command is installed: install.sh has finished with "Next step: sudo aifw setup". See The installer script.
  • The registry is reachable: versions, setup and upgrade need to reach the software registry. The other commands work offline.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Group Command What it does Changes the server? Before you install or upgrade aifw versions Lists the server versions available to install No Setting up and repairing aifw setup Sets up the server, guided Yes aifw setup --check Shows what setup would do No aifw setup --answers <file> Sets up with no questions, reading answers from a file Yes Moving to a newer version aifw upgrade [--version <v>] Moves the server to a newer version. Backs up first, keeps data Yes Checking a running server aifw status Is everything healthy? No aifw security-audit Checks the security posture No aifw doctor A full check-up with numbered findings and fixes No Backing up aifw backup Backs up the database and settings now Yes (adds files only) The tool itself aifw --version Prints the version of aifw No aifw --help Prints the help (also what you get with no arguments) No aifw preflight The machine checks on their own. setup runs them for you No

The marks in the output are the same everywhere: ✓ passed, ! a recommendation, ✗ a requirement that is not met.

docs.title: aifw versions
docs.text:
Lists the versions that the software registry holds, newest first. Changes nothing.

A version that is not in the list cannot be installed or upgraded to. If the version you need is missing, it has not been published yet: wait for it, or contact support. Older versions stay in the list and stay installable.

# aifw versions
Available server versions (newest first):
2.2.6
2.2.5
2.0.75

docs.title: aifw setup
docs.text:
Run this after install.sh has finished. It performs the installation, and it is also the repair command.

The order:

  1. The questions. It asks for the server type, the public address, how HTTPS works, the version, whether the emergency token field appears on the sign-in page, the license file, your email, the name of the first workspace, and an optional limit on SSH addresses. It then prints the answers back and asks for a yes. Nothing on the server has changed yet.
  2. The machine checks. If a requirement is not met, setup stops and prints what to fix. Nothing has changed yet.
  3. The phases, one at a time, printing each step as it runs.
  4. The security posture. The checks that did not pass, each with a fix. The installation has already succeeded. These are open items, not failures.

Running it again is safe. Each step looks at the server before it changes anything, so a second run changes only what has drifted. The questions offer your previous answers.

setup is the only command that configures the sign-in service. When a check says the administrator sign-in failed, run sudo aifw setup. An upgrade does not do this.

[TBC: product team to confirm what happens when you re-run setup with a changed answer, for example another public address. The installation runbook says to restore the snapshot first.]

Options:

  • --check prints what would change and changes nothing. Use it before a repeat run on a live server.
  • --answers <file> runs without questions, reading the answers from a file. See Install the server.

Also: setup turns on the automatic security updates of the system.

docs.title: aifw upgrade
docs.text:
Moves the server to a newer version. It takes a backup first, and your data stays.

Run it without --version to take the newest published version. Run it with --version 2.2.5 to take a named one.

Four limits:

  1. It cannot reach a version that is not published. Run aifw versions first. If the target is the version already running, it stops with This server is already on <version> — nothing to do. Nothing was changed.
  2. It does not go backwards. Database changes only move forward. A typing mistake in a version number is enough to try a downgrade, so the refusal is a stop, not a warning.
  3. It does not set up sign-in. The server keeps the sign-in setup it had. Run sudo aifw setup for that.
  4. It does not move third-party software. The database, the sign-in service, the web front end and the monitoring stay where they are. They move when the product pins newer versions of them.

The run ends with the security posture, the same list that security-audit prints.

Upgrade the server before the agents

Deploy the server first, or at the same time as the first agent of a new version. An older server drops the parts of a newer agent's data that it does not recognise. It can also report findings that are not findings. Nothing checks the order for you.

Two lines are worth recognising:

The installer updated itself — continuing the upgrade with the new version
This server is already on <version> — nothing to do

The first means the tool replaced its own program and ran once more. That is normal. The second is a success: nothing newer is published.

[TBC: bring the full upgrade procedure (the five steps, choosing a version, rolling back) from the product notes into Operate and upgrade.]

docs.title: Checking a running server
docs.text:
Three commands, three questions:

  • aifw status: is the server working?
  • aifw security-audit: is it safe?
  • aifw doctor: both, plus the machine checks, with a fix beside each finding.

docs.title: aifw status
docs.text:
Reports whether the server is working. Changes nothing.

It runs the health checks that the stack performs on itself, then prints the services, the free disk space, the age of the last backup, whether the sign-in address matches the configuration, and how long the web certificate is still valid.

One health check would create a workspace. status skips it and says so.

# aifw status
Server status:
Server check:
✓ Server configuration present
✓ All services running — 7 services up
✓ Health checks — PASSED: 24 FAILED: 0
✓ Free disk space — 81 GB free
✓ Recent backup (under 26 hours old) — backup-2026-09-30T00-27-04.sql.gz, 7.3 h old
✓ Sign-in service address matches the configuration
✓ Web certificate validity — expires in 633 day(s)

docs.title: aifw security-audit
docs.text:
Reports the security posture. Changes nothing.

It checks the firewall, file permissions, license enforcement, demo accounts, the stored registry sign-in and pending system updates.

The last line says This server is not ready yet in two different cases: a posture that is not hardened, or a check that could not run at all. The ✗ rows say which. could not check means nothing is known either way. It is not a pass.

Abridged example. The long "What to do" texts are shortened:

# aifw security-audit
Security posture:
Server check:
✓ Server configuration present
✓ Firewall enabled, incoming denied by default
! SSH password sign-in disabled (keys only)
What to do: Consider key-only SSH …
! SSH reachable only from addresses you trust — port 22 accepts connections from any address
What to do: Restrict SSH to the addresses your administrators use …
✓ Configuration and credentials are administrator-only
! Credentials sheet moved to a password manager — credentials.txt still on the server
What to do: Move its contents to your password manager, then delete credentials.txt.
✓ License enforced with the built-in verification key — license active
✓ Registry sign-in — this must be a READ-ONLY access token, never a publishing one
✗ No demo accounts in the sign-in service — could not check
What to do: This check could not run, so nothing is known either way …
! System packages current — 10 update(s) pending
What to do: Automatic security updates are on; a reboot may be needed …
This server is not ready yet: 1 requirement(s) unmet, 4 recommendation(s).

docs.title: aifw doctor
docs.text:
Runs everything that status and security-audit run, plus the machine checks. Prints the result as numbered findings, each with its fix. Changes nothing.

Run it when something is wrong and you want a list of actions, or when you do not know which of the three to use.

docs.title: aifw backup
docs.text:
Dumps the database and the settings. The database of the sign-in service is included. Dumps older than 30 days are deleted.

Set AIFW_BACKUP_REMOTE and the dump is also copied off the machine. setup installs a timer that takes a backup every day. upgrade takes one before anything moves. Run the command by hand before a risky change.

It adds files and deletes its own old dumps. Nothing else is written.

# aifw backup
Backing up the database (this can take a minute)...
Note: backups live only on this server. An off-server copy protects against losing the machine.
Backup done: /opt/ai-firewall/backups/backup-2026-10-06T08-45-59.sql.gz (0.1 MB)

The note appears when AIFW_BACKUP_REMOTE is not set. A settings file is written beside the dump with the same time stamp. See Backup and restore for what else to save and how to restore.

docs.title: aifw --version
docs.text:
Prints the version of the aifw program on this machine. That is not always the version the server runs: the two drift apart when the program is left behind. An old program then reports services as missing, because it looks for containers that a newer stack has retired.

# aifw --version
aifw 2.2.6

docs.title: aifw --help
docs.text: Lists every command with a one-line description. aifw with no arguments prints the same.

docs.title: aifw preflight
docs.text:
Runs the machine checks on their own, without starting an installation. Changes nothing. setup runs the same checks as its first step and stops if a requirement is not met, so there is rarely a reason to type it. On a running server, doctor includes it.

It checks: administrator rights, machine type, operating system, number of processors, memory (4 GB minimum, 8 GB recommended), free disk space (20 GB minimum), systemd, Docker installed and running, Docker Compose, whether the registry can be reached, and ports 80, 443 and 8090.

# aifw preflight
Server check:
✓ Administrator rights
✓ Machine type — this machine is x86_64
✓ Operating system — Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
✓ Processors — 2 available
✓ Memory (minimum 4 GB) — 7.8 GB installed
✓ Memory (recommended 8 GB) — 7.8 GB installed
✓ Free disk space (minimum 20 GB) — 82 GB free
✓ Service manager (systemd)
✓ Docker installed and running
✓ Docker Compose available
✓ Software registry reachable
✓ Web ports free (80, 443, 8090)

On a server that is already running, the ports check recognises the product's own services and names them. A ports warning means another program holds the port.

docs.text: Symptom Likely cause What to do setup stops on the server check, before asking anything The machine is short of memory or disk, or cannot reach the registry Each ✗ row names the fix. Nothing was changed. Fix it, then run sudo aifw setup again The chosen version does not exist in the registry That version was never published Run aifw versions. It lists everything that can be installed This server is already on a version — nothing to do upgrade resolved to the version already running Nothing is wrong. The newer version is not published yet The version is OLDER than the version this server runs A downgrade, usually a typing mistake Check the version.
