docs.title: Backup and restore
docs.text:
This page explains what to back up, how to make a backup, and how to bring the server back from one.

Never run docker compose down -v on a server

It deletes the data volumes, including the database. Use docker compose stop or down without -v. Nothing on this page removes a volume.

Restore is a manual procedure

The product has a backup command (aifw backup) but no restore command. The restore steps below are put together from how the server works. They have been proven only in part. Rehearse the whole procedure on a test server before you rely on it.

[TBC: product team to confirm the restore procedure, and to say whether a restore command is planned.]

docs.title: What holds your data
docs.text:
What Where What it holds Priority Saved by aifw backup Database ai_firewall volume pg-data Workspaces, devices, enrolment keys, policies, admin users, audit records and their chain, conversations, statistics Critical Yes Database keycloak the same volume People, groups, one-time codes, clients and the signing keys of the sign-in service Critical Yes Database roles the same volume The database accounts and their password hashes Critical Yes The settings file .env docker/.env in the install folder Every credential and shared secret of the server, the license, the image versions, the public address Critical A copy is kept on the server only Captured data volume capture-data Per-workspace capture data and approved destinations High No Generated briefs volume briefs-data Generated discovery files Medium No Policy presets, secrets folder presets/, secrets/ in the install folder Policy presets, optional secret files High No Your own TLS certificate docker/caddy/certs/ The certificate and key, if you chose your own certificate Medium. A Let's Encrypt certificate can be issued again No Installation files the install folder provision-manifest.json, credentials.txt if you kept it, proxy-snippets/ Medium No Registry sign-in /root/.docker/config.json The access that lets aifw upgrade download images Medium. It can be issued again No Metrics volumes prometheus-data, grafana-data Metrics for 30 days and dashboard settings Low No

What you do not need to back up: the containers (they are rebuilt from the images), the device certificates and private keys (they exist only on each computer; the server keeps public keys only, and these are in the database), and encryption keys (the server has none).

docs.title: Why .env must travel with the database
docs.text: A database dump alone cannot be restored into a working server. The dump restores the database account password hashes, and the passwords in .env must match them. The keys of the sign-in service and the shared secrets in .env must match the restored database too. Keep the .env copy as carefully as a password vault. It holds every credential of the server.

docs.title: Make a backup
docs.text: All commands run on the server, with sudo.

docs.title: What aifw backup does
docs.text:
sudo aifw backup
  1. Dumps both databases and all roles into /opt/ai-firewall/backups/backup-<time>.sql.gz. A failed or empty dump is deleted, and the command fails.
  2. Copies docker/.env to /opt/ai-firewall/backups/backup-<time>.env, readable by the administrator only.
  3. Deletes its own backups older than 30 days.
  4. If AIFW_BACKUP_REMOTE is set, copies only the .sql.gz file to that place with scp. A failed copy shows a warning.

The .env copy stays on the server. Move it to your backup storage yourself.

aifw upgrade makes the same backup before it changes anything, and stops if the backup fails.

docs.title: Set it up once
docs.text:
1. Choose a place outside the server. Add this line to /opt/ai-firewall/docker/.env, and make sure the administrator's SSH key is allowed on that machine:

    AIFW_BACKUP_REMOTE=<user>@<backup-host>:/path/to/backups/

  2. Turn on the daily schedule. Setup already does this. To install it again:

    sudo aifw backup --install-timer
systemctl list-timers aifw-backup.timer

    It runs once a day, with a random delay of up to an hour, and catches up after a restart.

  3. Run a first backup now, and look at the result:

    sudo aifw backup
ls -lh /opt/ai-firewall/backups/

docs.title: Save what aifw backup does not
docs.text:
Copy the volumes and files from the table above, and move the .env copy and the archives off the server.

STACK=/opt/ai-firewall/docker
BK=/var/backups/ai-firewall/$(date +%F_%H%M)
sudo mkdir -p "$BK" && sudo chmod 700 "$BK"

# the data volumes
for v in capture-data briefs-data; do
  sudo docker run --rm -v ai-firewall_${v}:/data:ro -v "$BK":/backup debian:stable-slim \
    tar czf /backup/${v}.tgz --numeric-owner -C /data .
done

# configuration, and the installation files
sudo tar czf "$BK/files.tgz" -C "$STACK" presets secrets caddy
sudo tar czf "$BK/install-files.tgz" -C /opt/ai-firewall provision-manifest.json proxy-snippets

Then copy $BK and the .env copy to storage outside the server.

docs.title: Check that a backup is good
docs.text: Check Expected The .sql.gz file Not empty, and gunzip -t finds no error. zgrep -c 'CREATE DATABASE' shows at least 2 The .env copy Present, readable by the administrator only The archives tar tzf lists the files without errors The copy outside the server Exists and is complete How fresh it is sudo aifw status and sudo aifw doctor warn when the newest backup is more than 26 hours old, or empty A restore drill A recent dump loads into a throw-away PostgreSQL 16 container with no errors except "already exists"

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Use the same or a newer version. The database is upgraded on start. A version older than the dump is not supported. The version is in the .env copy.
  • Keep the same public address. The address is stored in the database, in the sign-in service and in .env, and the agents have it in their settings. Changing it is not covered here.
  • The order matters. Load the databases before the sign-in service and the server start against them. Otherwise the sign-in service creates a new empty realm, and the server migrates an empty database. Setup and upgrade start everything at once, so load the database by hand.
  • You need: the database dump, the .env copy, the volume and file archives, and the registry access details from your welcome email.

Variables used below:

STACK=/opt/ai-firewall/docker
BK=/path/to/the/unpacked/backup
COMPOSE="docker compose --project-directory $STACK --env-file $STACK/.env -f $STACK/docker-compose.prod.yml"
# with bundled HTTPS, add:  -f $STACK/docker-compose.tls.yml
PG_USER=ai_firewall        # or the PG_USER value from the .env copy

docs.title: Scenario A: a new server
docs.text:
1. Prepare the server. Ubuntu 24.04, the same network rules as the old one. Install the same version of the setup tool with install.sh.

  2. Put the .env back before you run setup. Setup never rewrites an existing .env. It only adds missing keys.

    sudo mkdir -p /opt/ai-firewall/docker
sudo install -m 600 "$BK"/backup-*.env /opt/ai-firewall/docker/.env
sudo tar xzf "$BK/files.tgz" -C "$STACK"
sudo tar xzf "$BK/install-files.tgz" -C /opt/ai-firewall

  3. Sign in to the registry with the access details from your welcome email, so the images can be downloaded.

  4. Start only the database, and wait until it is ready. On an empty volume it starts, restarts once and sets itself up, so wait twice:

    $COMPOSE up -d postgres
until docker exec ai-firewall-pg pg_isready -U $PG_USER; do sleep 2; done
sleep 5
until docker exec ai-firewall-pg pg_isready -U $PG_USER; do sleep 2; done

  5. Load the dump (see Load the database dump).

  6. Restore the data volumes. Create them first, then unpack:

    $COMPOSE up --no-start
for v in capture-data briefs-data; do
  docker run --rm -v ai-firewall_${v}:/data -v "$BK":/backup debian:stable-slim \
    sh -c "tar xzf /backup/${v}.tgz --numeric-owner -C /data && chown -R 10005:10005 /data"
done

  7. Start everything, then run setup again to put back the host settings (the backup timer and the checks). It finds the existing .env and keeps it:

    $COMPOSE up -d
sudo aifw setup

  8. Point traffic at the new server. Change the DNS record, or the target of your load balancer or proxy.

  9. Check (see Check after a restore). Switch off the old server only when the checks pass.

[TBC: confirm the steps for loading images and for running setup again after a restore.]

docs.title: Scenario B: the same server, damaged data
docs.text:
1. Take a safety dump of the current state first. It is the only way back if the restore goes wrong:

    sudo aifw backup

  2. Stop everything except the database. Do not use down -v:

    $COMPOSE stop control-plane keycloak admin-portal grafana prometheus

  3. Put back the matching .env if it changed since the backup (for example after credentials were changed):

    sudo install -m 600 "$BK"/backup-*.env "$STACK/.env"
$COMPOSE up -d postgres

  4. Load the dump (next section).

  5. Restore files and volumes only if they are damaged, as in Scenario A, step 6.
  6. Start the server with the same or a newer version: $COMPOSE up -d. Then check.

docs.title: Load the database dump
docs.text:
The dump already holds the commands that create the roles and both databases. Remove the existing databases first, then load the dump while connected to the maintenance database:

docker exec -i ai-firewall-pg psql -U $PG_USER -d postgres <<'SQL'
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE datname IN ('ai_firewall','keycloak') AND pid <> pg_backend_pid();
DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS keycloak;
DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ai_firewall;
SQL

gunzip -c "$BK"/backup-*.sql.gz | docker exec -i ai-firewall-pg psql -U $PG_USER -d postgres 2>&1 | tee /tmp/restore.log
grep -i error /tmp/restore.log

Expected error: role "ai_firewall" already exists. Later lines still set the right password hash. Any other error means the restore is incomplete. Stop, find the cause, and go back to the safety dump if needed.

Quick check before you start the rest:

docker exec ai-firewall-pg psql -U $PG_USER -d ai_firewall -c "SELECT count(*) FROM tenants;"
docker exec ai-firewall-pg psql -U $PG_USER -d keycloak -c "SELECT name FROM realm;"

The first must give the number of workspaces you expect. The second must list master and ai-firewall.

docs.title: Check after a restore
docs.text: # Check Command Expected 1 Containers are healthy docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}' The database, sign-in service, portal and server are healthy 2 The server is alive curl -fsS http://localhost:8090/health {"status":"ok"} 3 The database is reachable curl -fsS http://localhost:8090/ready {"status":"ready"} 4 The database was upgraded docker logs ai-firewall-control-plane 2>&1 \| grep -i migrat Pending changes applied, no failure 5 The built-in checks sudo aifw status && sudo aifw doctor All pass, including the sign-in address and the backup age 6 The sign-in address curl -fsS https://<your-address>/keycloak/realms/ai-firewall/.well-known/openid-configuration The issuer starts with your public address 7 The console is closed curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://<your-address>/keycloak/admin/ 404 8 The portal Sign in at https://<your-address>/admin/ Your workspaces, devices and policies are there 9 The audit chain The chain check in the portal It verifies. A gap from the restore shows as a re-anchor, not as tampering 10 Agents The device list in the portal Devices report again within minutes

docs.title: What agents experience after a restore
docs.text:
• Computers enrolled before the backup reconnect with their existing keys. Nothing to do.
  • Computers enrolled after the backup are refused at first. The agent then drops its key and joins again by itself with its enrolment key. This works only if the enrolment keys did not change, which is another reason to restore the original .env.
  • Audit events between the backup and the failure are lost on the server, unless agents still hold them and send them again. The gap is recorded as a re-anchor.
  • Changes made in the portal after the backup (policies, groups, administrators, sign-in accounts and one-time codes) are lost and must be done again.

docs.title: Single sign-on with your company directory
docs.text:
An identity provider (IdP) lets people sign in to the admin portal with the accounts they already have, for example their Microsoft Entra ID account.

[TBC: the product notes call this federation a preview. Decide whether to publish this page, and with what warning.]

docs.title: Why use one
docs.text:
• One account and one password. People do not get a separate portal password, and you do not have to deliver passwords.
  • Central account life. When your organisation disables an employee in the directory, that person can no longer sign in to the portal.
  • Your sign-in rules. Multi-factor sign-in, conditional access and password rules of the IdP apply to the portal.

The IdP only confirms who the person is. Keycloak still decides what they can do: the role, the workspace group and all-workspace access are set in the ai-firewall realm, in the same way as for local accounts. See Sign-in and roles.

docs.title: How single sign-on works
docs.text: A person opens https://<your-address>/admin. They are sent to the Keycloak sign-in page, choose the IdP, sign in there and return to the portal. Keycloak sits between the portal and the IdP.

docs.title: Steps for any provider
docs.text:
1. Add the IdP to the ai-firewall realm only. Never to master.
  2. Choose the alias first, for example entra-id. The alias is part of the redirect address and cannot be changed after you create the provider.

  3. Register Keycloak as an application in the IdP. The redirect address is:

    https://<your-address>/keycloak/realms/ai-firewall/broker/<alias>/endpoint

    Do not copy the redirect address that the Keycloak console shows. The console opens through an SSH tunnel and shows an address that starts with http://127.0.0.1. The IdP and the users' browsers cannot reach it. Take the value from the console and replace the part before /keycloak with your public address.

  4. Create the provider in Keycloak with the client ID and the client secret from the IdP.

  5. Plan how people get access. A person who signs in through the IdP for the first time is created in the ai-firewall realm without a role and without a workspace group, so the portal does not work for them yet. Either give them the role and the group by hand after the first sign-in, or add mappers that do it automatically. Never map anyone to fleet-operators automatically.
  6. Test with a test account before you tell people: open the portal, choose the IdP, and check that the person sees the right workspace.
  7. Optional: skip the Keycloak page. Set the IdP as the default provider of the Identity Provider Redirector step in the browser authentication flow of the realm. Keep at least one local administrator account for when the IdP is not available.

docs.title: Microsoft Entra ID
docs.text:
You can connect Entra ID in two ways. Both use an app registration in Entra ID.

Built-in Microsoft provider Generic OpenID Connect provider Effort Low: client ID, client secret and tenant ID Higher: discovery address, client authentication, scopes, signature checks Map Entra groups or app roles to Keycloak Not supported Supported, with mappers Limit to your organisation Only if you fill in the tenant ID. An empty field lets any Microsoft account in Built in Choose it when People only need to sign in, and you give roles and groups in Keycloak You want Entra groups or app roles to give access

docs.title: Option 1. Built-in Microsoft provider
docs.text:
In the Microsoft Entra admin center:

  1. Open App registrations, then New registration.
  2. Enter a name, for example AI Firewall admin portal. For Supported account types, choose Accounts in this organizational directory only.
  3. For Redirect URI, choose the Web platform and enter the redirect address from above. Select Register.
  4. On Overview, copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID.
  5. Open Certificates & secrets, create a new client secret and copy its Value. Note the expiry date: sign-in stops when the secret expires.
  6. In API permissions, check that the delegated Microsoft Graph permission User.Read is there.

In the Keycloak console (realm ai-firewall):

  1. Open Identity providers and choose Microsoft.
  2. Fill in Alias, Display name (the text of the button on the sign-in page), Client ID, Client Secret and Tenant ID. Do not leave Tenant ID empty.
  3. Select Add.

docs.title: Option 2. Generic OpenID Connect provider
docs.text:
In the Microsoft Entra admin center:

  1. Register the application as in steps 1 to 5 above, with the same redirect address.
  2. Open Token configuration and add the optional claim email to the ID token.
  3. To pass Entra groups, select Add groups claim. To pass app roles, define them in App roles and assign people to them in Enterprise applications.

In the Keycloak console (realm ai-firewall):

  1. Open Identity providers and choose OpenID Connect v1.0.
  2. Fill in Alias and Display name.
  3. For Discovery endpoint, enter https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration.
  4. Set Client authentication to Client secret sent as post. Fill in Client ID and Client Secret.
  5. Select Add. Then set Scopes to openid profile email, make sure Validate Signatures and Use JWKS URL are on, and select Save.
  6. If Entra passes groups or app roles, open Mappers and add Claim to Role or Advanced Claim to Group mappers that turn them into the role and the workspace group.

docs.title: After you connect
docs.text:
• Without mappers, give each new person the role and the workspace group by hand.
  • Never map Entra groups or roles to fleet-operators automatically.
  • Before the client secret expires, create a new one in Entra ID and update Client Secret in the provider.

docs.title: More information
docs.text:
• Keycloak: Server Administration Guide, the sections on identity providers and mappers.
  • Microsoft: Register an application and OpenID Connect on the Microsoft identity platform.

docs.title: The installer script: install.sh
docs.text:
install.sh is the first step of installing the ScienceSoft AI Endpoint Firewall server. It prepares an empty Ubuntu server and installs one command, aifw. You then run aifw setup, which installs and configures everything else: the server, the admin portal, the sign-in service, the database, HTTPS and monitoring.

sudo bash install.sh
sudo aifw setup

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
File What it is install.sh The installer script README.txt The same instructions as on this page, as a text file to keep next to the script SHA256SUMS The checksum of install.sh, to check that the file is intact

You need the registry access name and token from your welcome email to run it. The software cannot be downloaded without them. The script does not contain them.

[TBC: product team to confirm that the script and the registry address inside it may be published openly.]

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An Ubuntu server. Ubuntu 24.04 LTS is the tested system. On another system the script prints a note and continues. Intel/AMD (x86_64) and ARM (aarch64) processors are supported.
  • Administrator rights (you run it with sudo).
  • Internet access from the server: to the Ubuntu package archive, to the software registry and, for Let's Encrypt, to the certificate authority.
  • The registry access name and token, and the license file, from your welcome email.
  • The server size and ports from Prerequisites.

Take a snapshot or backup of the server first.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Copy install.sh to the server. If you copied it from a Windows computer, convert the line endings first, or it can fail without a message:

    sed -i 's/\r$//' install.sh

  2. Check that the file is intact. Put install.sh and SHA256SUMS in the same folder. The result must be OK:

    sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

  3. Run the script as administrator:

    sudo bash install.sh

  4. When asked, enter the registry access name and the access token. The token you type is hidden. They are checked at once.

  5. Wait for the script to finish. It ends with:

    Done. The aifw command is installed:
aifw <version>

Next step:  sudo aifw setup

  6. Check the server, then set it up. See Install the server and the aifw command reference:

    sudo aifw preflight
sudo aifw setup

docs.title: What the script does
docs.text:
1. Checks that you run it as administrator.
  2. Notes the operating system. It continues on a system other than Ubuntu 24.04.
  3. Checks the processor type. Anything other than x86_64 or aarch64 stops the script before anything is changed.
  4. Installs Docker Engine and the Docker Compose component if they are missing. Docker comes from the Ubuntu package archive.
  5. Signs in to the software registry with your access name and token, and checks them.
  6. Downloads the installer image for this processor type and takes the aifw command out of it.
  7. Puts aifw at /usr/local/bin/aifw and prints its version.

It does not set up the server. That is aifw setup.

The registry sign-in is stored for the administrator account (root) in Docker's settings, so that aifw upgrade can download newer versions later. The access token should be a read-only token.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
For an unattended installation, give the script its settings as environment variables. All are optional, except the two access values, which the script asks for when they are not set.

Variable Meaning AIFW_REGISTRY_USER The registry access name AIFW_REGISTRY_TOKEN The registry access token AIFW_VERSION The version of the installer to download. By default: the version this server already runs, or latest on a new server AIFW_REGISTRY The software registry address (set by default) AIFW_REGISTRY_PATH The project in the registry (set by default)

Example, with no questions asked:

sudo AIFW_REGISTRY_USER='<name>' AIFW_REGISTRY_TOKEN='<token>' bash install.sh

A command line is not private

Other users of the server can see a command line for a moment, and it can stay in the shell history. Prefer the questions on the screen, unless the installation is automated and the secret comes from a secret store.

To install a specific version:

sudo AIFW_VERSION=<version> bash install.sh

Running the script again is safe. It repairs a damaged aifw command. On a server that already runs the product it keeps the version the server runs, unless you set AIFW_VERSION.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
The script stops with a line that starts with "Problem:".

The message says What to do This installer needs administrator rights Run it with sudo: sudo bash install.sh The software is published for Intel/AMD (x86_64) and ARM (aarch64) servers The server has another processor type. Use a supported server Another program is installing software right now Often the automatic security updater, just after boot. Wait a minute and run the script again This server could not reach the Ubuntu package archive Check the internet access and proxy settings of the server Both the access name and the token are needed Both are in your welcome email. Ask your ScienceSoft contact if you cannot find them The registry did not accept the access token Check for typing mistakes. If it still fails, ask for a new token Could not download the installer image Check the internet access of the server to the software registry This version was not published for this machine There is no build for this processor type. Ask your ScienceSoft contact, or use an Intel/AMD server Could not write the aifw command The disk is full or read-only. Check it with df -h /usr/local/bin Docker is installed but not running Start it with systemctl start docker

After you fix the cause, run the script again. For problems with setup, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• Read the script before you run it as administrator. It is a short, plain shell script.
  • Download it only from this site or from your welcome email, and check the checksum.
  • Keep the access token secret. Do not put it into tickets or chats.

docs.title: Install the server
docs.text: This page takes you from an empty Ubuntu server to a working AI Firewall server. Read Prerequisites first.

docs.title: Step 1. Prepare the server
docs.text:
Connect over SSH and become the administrator:

ssh <user>@<server-address>
sudo -i
cd <folder that holds install.sh>
chmod +x ./install.sh

If you copied install.sh from a Windows computer

A script saved with Windows line endings can fail silently on Linux. Convert it before you run it:

sed -i 's/\r$//' install.sh

docs.title: Step 2. Install Docker and the aifw command
docs.text:
bash install.sh

The script:

  1. installs Docker Engine and the Docker Compose plugin, if they are missing;
  2. asks for the registry access name and token from your welcome email (what you type is hidden) and checks them at once;
  3. downloads the setup tool and installs the aifw command.

Check that it worked:

aifw --version

To install a specific version of the aifw command, set AIFW_VERSION when you run the script, for example AIFW_VERSION=<version> bash install.sh. By default the script takes the version that this server already runs, or the newest version on a new server. All the settings of the script and its error messages are on The installer script. Every aifw command is described on aifw commands.

docs.title: Step 3. Check the server (optional, recommended)
docs.text:
aifw preflight

It checks the processor, memory and disk, that the needed ports are free, that systemd is present and that the server can reach the software registry. It changes nothing. A problem shows up here instead of half way through setup. Run it before a non-interactive installation, when nobody watches the questions.

docs.title: Step 4. Run setup
docs.text:
Setup creates and starts everything. You can run it in two ways.

Interactive. Setup asks the questions one by one and shows a summary to confirm before it changes anything:

aifw setup

Non-interactive. Setup reads the answers from a file, so an installation is repeatable:

aifw setup --answers /opt/ai-firewall/answers.json

Unknown keys in the file are rejected with an error, so a typing mistake fails loudly. Passwords and tokens are never part of this file. They are always generated for your server.

To see the whole plan without changing anything:

aifw setup --check

Whichever way you run it, setup goes through eight phases: server check, server preparation, your answers, configuration and generated secrets, download and start, secure web access, sign-in service set-up, and the final sign-in details and backup set-up. It reports what it created and what was already in place.

Running setup again is safe

Each step looks at the server before it changes anything, so a second run changes only what has drifted. Your previous answers are offered again. Use aifw setup --check first on a live server: it shows what would change and changes nothing.

Before you change a basic answer

If a basic answer has to change (the public address, the HTTPS handling, the version or the license), take a snapshot of the server first.

[TBC: product team to confirm how setup behaves when a basic answer is changed. The installation runbook says to restore the pre-installation snapshot first; the command reference and the quick start say a repeat run is safe.]

docs.title: The answers
docs.text: Answer Prompt What it is flavor Server type standard for a normal installation. publicUrl Public address The full https:// address of the server. No path, no trailing slash. version Version The exact version to install, for example 2.2.7. Not latest. authMode Emergency token field on the sign-in page compat: the sign-in page has the single sign-on button and an emergency token field (recommended). keycloak: single sign-on only. licenseBlobPath License file path The full path of the .license file on the server. adminEmail Admin email The first administrator. A temporary password is made and shown once at the end. workspaceId First workspace name main, unless you need another name. adminSshSourceIp Restrict SSH to one address Optional. Lets only this address connect over SSH. hardenSsh (answers file only) Optional. true turns off SSH sign-in by password. Default false. rootDir (answers file only) Where the installation lives. Default /opt/ai-firewall.

docs.title: How HTTPS is handled
docs.text: One more answer decides how the server gets its HTTPS certificate. It is called HTTPS handling in the questions and tlsMode in the answers file.

docs.title: Option 1. Automatic certificates (Let's Encrypt)
docs.text:
Choose this when the server has a public DNS name that is reachable from the internet, and you want the certificate to be issued and renewed automatically.

Key Value tlsMode caddy-letsencrypt letsencryptEmail The contact address for certificate notices

Port 80 must be open, as well as 443. The DNS name must already point at this server, because the certificate authority checks it during setup.

{
  "flavor": "standard",
  "publicUrl": "https://ai-firewall.example.com",
  "version": "<version>",
  "authMode": "compat",
  "licenseBlobPath": "/opt/ai-firewall/company.license",
  "adminEmail": "admin@example.com",
  "workspaceId": "main",
  "tlsMode": "caddy-letsencrypt",
  "letsencryptEmail": "admin@example.com",
  "hardenSsh": false
}

docs.title: Option 2. Your own certificate
docs.text:
Choose this when you have your own certificate, for example from a company certificate authority, or when the server has no public DNS name.

Key Value tlsMode caddy-custom tlsCertPath The full path of the certificate (.pem) on the server tlsKeyPath The full path of its private key

Put the certificate and key on the server before you start, at those paths, readable by the user who runs setup. Port 80 is not needed.

{
  "flavor": "standard",
  "publicUrl": "https://ai-firewall.example.com",
  "version": "<version>",
  "authMode": "compat",
  "licenseBlobPath": "/opt/ai-firewall/company.license",
  "adminEmail": "admin@example.com",
  "workspaceId": "main",
  "tlsMode": "caddy-custom",
  "tlsCertPath": "/opt/ai-firewall/certs/server.pem",
  "tlsKeyPath": "/opt/ai-firewall/certs/server.key",
  "hardenSsh": false
}

docs.title: Option 3. Your own load balancer or proxy
docs.text:
Choose this when a load balancer or reverse proxy in front of the server already ends HTTPS, and only plain HTTP reaches the server. This is usual in a company network or behind a managed load balancer in a cloud.

Key Value tlsMode external lbIp Optional. The address of the load balancer, to allow it through the firewall

Set up and start the load balancer before you run setup. Setup also writes ready-made settings for nginx and IIS that you can use. See Reverse proxy.

{
  "flavor": "standard",
  "publicUrl": "https://ai-firewall.example.com",
  "version": "<version>",
  "authMode": "compat",
  "licenseBlobPath": "/opt/ai-firewall/company.license",
  "adminEmail": "admin@example.com",
  "workspaceId": "main",
  "tlsMode": "external",
  "lbIp": "<load-balancer-ip>",
  "hardenSsh": false
}

docs.title: Step 5. Check that it works
docs.text:
docker ps

All containers must show Up, and (healthy) once their start-up time has passed:

Container What it does ai-firewall-caddy Handles HTTPS on ports 80 and 443 (not present when you use your own load balancer) ai-firewall-control-plane The server itself: devices, administration and audit. Listens on port 8090 inside the server ai-firewall-admin-portal The admin portal ai-firewall-keycloak The sign-in service ai-firewall-pg The database ai-firewall-prometheus, ai-firewall-grafana Metrics and dashboards ai-firewall-postgres-exporter, ai-firewall-blackbox Monitoring helpers

[TBC: confirm the container names and the list for the current version.]

From the server, ask the service if it is healthy:

curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8090/health
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8090/ready

Or run:

aifw status

Then, from outside:

  • health: https://<your-address>/health must answer {"status":"ok"};
  • the sign-in page: https://<your-address>/admin.

docs.title: Step 6. Save the sign-in details
docs.text:
Setup writes the sign-in details to credentials.txt in the install folder, for example /opt/ai-firewall/credentials.txt. They are also shown on the last screen. The file holds:

  • the address of the admin portal, the administrator's email and a temporary password;
  • the device enrolment key, which the agent installers use to join computers to your workspace;
  • the emergency sign-in token;
  • the monitoring dashboard password;
  • the sign-in service console account and the command to reach the console (see Sign-in and roles).

Move every value into your password manager now, then delete the file:

rm /opt/ai-firewall/credentials.txt

Other secrets that the installation needs (the database password, internal tokens and the license) are generated into a file that only the administrator can read, in the install folder. Keep it on the server. Do not copy it, and never paste it into a ticket or a chat.

docs.title: Step 7. Check the firewall of the server
docs.text:
ufw status verbose

Only the ports for your HTTPS option (see Prerequisites) should be open. Everything else is blocked.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Sign-in and roles: sign in and add administrators.
  • Operate and upgrade: turn on backups.

docs.title: Operate and upgrade
docs.text: All commands run on the server, as the administrator (use sudo).

docs.title: Everyday commands
docs.text:
Command What it does aifw status Shows whether everything is healthy. Safe to run at any time. aifw doctor Looks for problems and explains what it finds. aifw security-audit Checks the security settings of the server. aifw versions Lists the versions you can upgrade to. aifw backup Makes a backup now. See Backup and restore. aifw --version Shows the version of the aifw command.

[TBC: confirm the exact output and purpose of doctor and security-audit for the current version.]

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
The database holds everything: workspaces, devices, audit history and usage statistics. Back it up and keep the backups away from the server.

sudo aifw backup
  • It writes a dated copy of both databases and a copy of the settings file (.env) into the backups folder under the install folder. It keeps the last 30 days.
  • Setup also installs a daily timer that runs the backup.
  • If you set AIFW_BACKUP_REMOTE, it copies the database dump only to that place. The copy of the settings file stays on the server. Move it to your backup storage yourself. A database dump alone cannot be restored without it.
  • Some data is not saved by aifw backup: captured data, policy presets and your own TLS certificate.

The full list, the steps for a complete backup and the restore procedure are on Backup and restore. There is no restore command: restoring is a manual procedure. Read it, and rehearse it on a test server, before you need it.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
sudo aifw versions               # what can I upgrade to?
sudo aifw upgrade --version <version>
sudo aifw status
  • Take a snapshot or a backup first. aifw upgrade also makes a backup before it changes anything, and stops if that backup fails.
  • The database is upgraded automatically. Updates are additive, so a server upgrade does not reject or lose data from computers that already use AI Firewall.
  • After the upgrade, check https://<your-address>/health.

docs.title: Roll back
docs.text:
If the new version does not work, go back to the previous one:

sudo aifw upgrade --version <previous-version>

There is no separate rollback command.

docs.title: Re-running setup
docs.text: Running aifw setup again is safe. It checks every part of the installation and repairs what has drifted, without touching your data, and offers your previous answers. Use aifw setup --check first to see what would change. If a basic answer must change (the public address, the HTTPS handling, the version or the license), take a snapshot first. See Install the server.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
The installation includes Grafana dashboards and Prometheus metrics. The Grafana password is in credentials.txt.

[TBC: describe how to open the dashboards and which alerts matter.]

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Have everything on this page ready before you start.

docs.title: What you receive from ScienceSoft
docs.text:
You get a welcome email. It contains:

  • the registry access details: a name and a token. The installer needs them to download the software;
  • the license file for your organisation (a file that ends in .license);
  • the installer script install.sh.

The software is not available for anonymous download. You need the registry access details to install it.

docs.title: The server
docs.text:
Minimum Recommended Operating system Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Intel/AMD (x86_64) or ARM (aarch64) Ubuntu 24.04 LTS CPU 2 vCPU 4 vCPU Memory 4 GB for the product itself, plus what the operating system needs 8 GB in total Free disk 20 GB 50 GB, and more as audit history grows Software systemd
  • The installer is tested on Ubuntu 24.04. On a newer release it continues, but shows a warning.
  • The installer adds Docker Engine and the Docker Compose plugin if they are missing.
  • The server needs a static IP address or a DHCP reservation.

docs.title: The network
docs.text: The server needs internet access during the installation. It downloads software from the vendor's private container registry and, depending on the version, from public container registries.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
The ports you need depend on how HTTPS is handled (see Install the server):

HTTPS handling Open inbound Notes Automatic certificates (Let's Encrypt) 22, 80, 443 Port 80 is used to issue the certificate. The server's DNS name must already point at this server. Your own certificate 22, 443 Your own load balancer or proxy 22, and 8090 only from the proxy's address You configure the proxy yourself. See Reverse proxy.

The ports must be free before setup. Setup turns on the server's firewall (ufw) with these rules.

[TBC: confirm the port list for each HTTPS mode with the product team.]

docs.title: A name for the server
docs.text: Choose the address users and devices will use, for example https://ai-firewall.example.com. It must be a full https:// address, with no path and no trailing slash. A DNS record for it must exist.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Take a snapshot or backup of the server. If you need to change an installation parameter later, restore the snapshot and run setup again from a clean state.
  2. Have the license file and the registry access details at hand.
  3. If you will use your own certificate, have the certificate and its key on the server, readable by the user who runs the installation.
  4. If you will use your own load balancer, set it up first. See Reverse proxy.
  5. Decide the email address of the first administrator.

docs.title: Tools on your own computer
docs.text: You need an SSH client to connect to the server, and a password manager to keep the sign-in details that setup shows once.

docs.title: Reverse proxy
docs.text:
Use this page when your own load balancer or reverse proxy ends HTTPS in front of the server (HTTPS option 3 in Install the server). Set the proxy up before you run setup, and before the first device connects.

You can use nginx, IIS, HAProxy, or a load balancer from your cloud provider.

docs.title: What the proxy must do
docs.text:
Requirement Value Public address HTTPS on port 443 for your server's name, with your certificate. HTTPS ends at the proxy Where it sends traffic Everything (/) to http://<server-ip>:8090 Server firewall Port 8090 open only to the proxy's address Headers Keep the original Host. Send X-Forwarded-Proto: https and X-Forwarded-Host: <your-name> WebSocket Pass the Upgrade and Connection headers through Timeouts An idle (read and send) timeout of 600 seconds or more Buffering Streamed responses (text/event-stream) must reach the client as they are written, not when the response ends

You do not need to do anything for the sign-in service console. The server refuses it on the public address. Administrators reach it through an SSH tunnel (see Sign-in and roles).

docs.title: Why these values
docs.text:
The server keeps long connections open:

  • Every managed computer keeps a stream open, so that a policy change reaches it at once. The server sends a keep-alive signal every 25 seconds.
  • The admin portal keeps streams open for audit records, with a keep-alive every 30 seconds.
  • One stream (the violations stream, for the top administrator role only) has no keep-alive yet.

Because of the keep-alive signals, a timeout of 60 seconds is enough for most streams. Setup generates 600 seconds, which also covers the stream without a keep-alive. A proxy that buffers responses holds events back, so computers get policy changes late. The server tells the proxy not to buffer its streams (X-Accel-Buffering: no).

docs.title: nginx
docs.text:
Setup writes this file for you when you choose your own proxy: <install folder>/proxy-snippets/nginx-server-block.conf. nginx waits only 60 seconds by default, so the two timeout lines are required.

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name ai-firewall.example.com;
    ssl_certificate     /path/to/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /path/to/privkey.pem;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://<server-ip>:8090;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host ai-firewall.example.com;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_read_timeout 600s;
        proxy_send_timeout 600s;
    }
}

nginx obeys the "do not buffer" header from the server, so you do not need another setting.

docs.title: IIS with URL Rewrite and ARR
docs.text:
Setup writes <install folder>/proxy-snippets/iis-web.config.

  1. Install the URL Rewrite and Application Request Routing (ARR) modules.

  2. Turn on the ARR proxy and set its timeout to 600 seconds or more. In IIS Manager, open the server node, then Application Request Routing Cache, then Server Proxy Settings. Or run:

    %windir%\system32\inetsrv\appcmd.exe set config -section:system.webServer/proxy /enabled:"True" /timeout:"00:10:00" /commit:apphost

    If computers receive policy changes late, set Response buffer threshold in the same place to 0.

  3. In the site's URL Rewrite settings, add HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO and HTTP_X_FORWARDED_HOST to the Allowed Server Variables. Without them the rule below fails.

  4. Bind the site to your name on HTTPS port 443 with your certificate, and add this rule:

    <configuration>
  <system.webServer>
    <rewrite>
      <rules>
        <rule name="proxy-to-ai-firewall" stopProcessing="true">
          <match url="(.*)" />
          <action type="Rewrite" url="http://<server-ip>:8090/{R:1}" />
          <serverVariables>
            <set name="HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO" value="https" />
            <set name="HTTP_X_FORWARDED_HOST" value="ai-firewall.example.com" />
          </serverVariables>
        </rule>
      </rules>
    </rewrite>
  </system.webServer>
</configuration>

[TBC: the buffer-threshold advice for IIS has not been verified in a customer environment.]

docs.title: HAProxy
docs.text:
Setup does not write a file for HAProxy. This is the equivalent of the nginx block. HAProxy does not buffer responses and passes WebSocket upgrades by itself. After the upgrade, timeout tunnel applies instead of timeout server.

frontend aifw_https
    mode http
    bind :443 ssl crt /etc/haproxy/certs/ai-firewall.pem
    timeout client 600s
    http-request set-header X-Forwarded-Proto https
    http-request set-header X-Forwarded-Host ai-firewall.example.com
    default_backend aifw_control_plane

backend aifw_control_plane
    mode http
    timeout server 600s
    timeout tunnel 600s
    option httpchk GET /health
    server cp1 <server-ip>:8090 check

docs.title: Check after you configure the proxy
docs.text:
curl -fsS https://ai-firewall.example.com/health

The answer must be {"status":"ok"}. Use your own name instead of ai-firewall.example.com, and your own server address instead of <server-ip>, everywhere on this page.

docs.title: Sign-in and roles
docs.text: This page explains who can sign in to AI Firewall, what each role can do, and how to add people.

docs.title: How people and devices are identified
docs.text:
AI Firewall uses Keycloak as its sign-in service. Keycloak runs as one of the containers of the server. It handles sign-in to the admin portal, roles and the sign-in log. It has two realms (separate sets of accounts):

Realm What it is for ai-firewall Sign-in to the admin portal. The role of a person decides what they can do. Their workspace group decides which workspace they see. master Sign-in to the Keycloak console, for the administrators who manage people and roles. What How it is identified People who use the admin portal Keycloak, realm ai-firewall Keycloak administrators Keycloak, realm master. One personal account for each administrator Computers (agents) Not through Keycloak. At first start the agent exchanges the device enrolment key for its own device key. Static tokens (the emergency sign-in token and the administration tokens) Not through Keycloak. They always have the highest rights and are not recorded in the sign-in log. Keep them for emergencies only.

docs.title: First sign-in
docs.text:
[screenshot: the admin portal sign-in page]

  1. Open https://<your-address>/admin.
  2. Select the single sign-on button. Sign in with the administrator email that you gave to setup and the temporary password from credentials.txt.
  3. You are asked to choose a new password.

If you set authMode to compat (the recommended value), the sign-in page also has an emergency token field. Use it only in an emergency, and keep the token in your password manager. With keycloak, the page has the single sign-on button only.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Every person who uses the admin portal has one base role. The server checks the role on every request, not only in the screens.

Role What it allows Who gets it admin Everything in their own workspace IT or security administrators who set up and run protection analyst Reading and investigating in their own workspace, without changes Analysts who review detections but must not change settings auditor Audit only: reading and export Auditors and compliance staff super-admin Added on top of a base role. All workspaces, creating workspaces, releases, platform audit and the sign-in log People who run the whole installation. Given only through the fleet-operators group

[TBC: the super-admin role is described in the product notes as being for ScienceSoft operators of a shared installation. Say who needs it on a server that belongs to one organisation, for example to create workspaces.]

A role is not enough. A person also needs a workspace group. Without it the portal shows no workspace.

docs.title: The default role
docs.text:
Give new portal users the auditor role. It has the fewest rights, so a person who gets it by mistake cannot change anything. Give analyst or admin only when the work needs it.

  • Do not add the product roles to the default roles of the ai-firewall realm. If you do, every new person, including people who sign in through a company directory, gets access automatically.
  • Never give super-admin by default, and never make fleet-operators a default group.

docs.title: Two accounts for an administrator
docs.text:
The Keycloak console and the admin portal use different realms, so an administrator who needs both has two accounts with the same username and separate passwords. Changing the password of one does not change the other. An account from the master realm cannot sign in to the admin portal. A person who needs the portal needs an account in the ai-firewall realm.

Use the built-in emergency administrator account only in an emergency, for example to create the first additional administrator. For regular work, create a personal administrator account for each person. Do not share one account.

docs.title: Open the Keycloak console
docs.text:
The console is never on the public address. Those addresses always answer "not found". You open it from your own computer through an SSH tunnel.

  1. In credentials.txt, find the console account and the tunnel command. The command looks like this:

    ssh -N -L 18080:127.0.0.1:8080 <user>@<server>

    Keep it running.

  2. Open http://127.0.0.1:18080/keycloak/admin/ in your browser. Use exactly that address, with 127.0.0.1, not localhost.

  3. Sign in with your master realm account. A one-time code from an authenticator app is required. The first time, you register the app. Every later sign-in asks for the code.
  4. Close the tunnel when you finish.

[TBC: the quick start that ships with the installer uses port 8080 on the server side of the tunnel. A separate server note for version 2.2.6 uses port 18080 and says a one-time server change is needed first. Confirm the correct command for the current version.]

docs.title: Add a person to the admin portal
docs.text:
[screenshot: Keycloak console: Add user, Credentials and Role mapping]

In the Keycloak console:

  1. Switch the realm (top left) from master to ai-firewall. A person created in master cannot sign in to the portal.
  2. Open Users, then Add user. Fill in the username, email and name. Turn on Email verified only if you have confirmed the address. Select Create.
  3. On the Credentials tab, select Set password. Enter a strong password and keep Temporary on, so the person must change it at the first sign-in.
  4. On the Role mapping tab, select Assign role, filter by realm roles, and choose one base role (admin, analyst or auditor).
  5. On the Groups tab, select Join group and choose the workspace group.

Deliver the password in a safe way:

  • Never send it in plain text by email, chat or in a ticket.
  • Send the username and the password through different channels, or use a password-sharing tool with a one-time link.
  • Ask the person to change the temporary password and to confirm when it is done.

super-admin is not given directly. Add the person to the fleet-operators group. To check, open Role mapping and turn off Hide inherited roles. A person with all-workspace access must show the base role and the inherited super-admin role. A person with one workspace must not show super-admin.

docs.title: The same from the command line
docs.text:
On the server, kcadm.sh runs inside the Keycloak container, so no tunnel is needed:

KC="sudo docker exec -it ai-firewall-keycloak /opt/keycloak/bin/kcadm.sh"
$KC config credentials --server http://localhost:8080/keycloak --realm master --user <your-admin-username>
$KC create users -r ai-firewall -s username=<email> -s email=<email> -s enabled=true
$KC set-password -r ai-firewall --username <email> --new-password '<temporary-password>' --temporary
$KC add-roles -r ai-firewall --uusername <email> --rolename admin

Then add the person to the workspace group in the console.

docs.title: Add a Keycloak administrator
docs.text:
1. In the console, make sure the realm is master.
  2. Open Users, then Add user, and set a temporary password as above.

  3. Give the access that fits:

    Scope Who needs it What to give The ai-firewall realm only An administrator who manages portal people, roles and groups Join the group aifw-realm-operators All realms, including master An administrator who replaces the emergency account for regular work The realm role admin of the master realm

For everyday work with portal people, the first scope is enough. Never create administrator accounts for the people who only use the portal.

docs.title: Connect your company's directory
docs.text: You can let people sign in with their company account, for example Microsoft Entra ID. See Single sign-on with your company directory.

docs.title: Required realm settings
docs.text:
Setup imports the ai-firewall realm when Keycloak starts for the first time. The realm has no people in it. These settings are required for the product to work. Do not change them.

Area Setting Required Roles admin, analyst, auditor, super-admin One base role for each person. super-admin is extra Groups fleet-operators Gives super-admin. Never a default group Groups Workspace groups Each has a tenant attribute. Every person must be in one Client admin-portal-spa A public client with PKCE S256. Direct access grants off. No client secret Client admin-api Bearer-only. No client secret Client admin-cli Do not change Login User registration Off

A running server does not read the realm file again. All other settings keep the Keycloak defaults.

[TBC: confirm with the product team that these names and settings are final for the current version.]

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
sudo aifw status
sudo aifw doctor
docker ps

aifw status says if the installation is healthy. docker ps shows each container. A container that is restarting or unhealthy is where to look first:

docker logs <container-name> --tail 200

docs.title: install.sh does nothing, or fails with a strange error
docs.text:
The script may have Windows line endings, for example if you copied it from a Windows computer. Convert it and run it again:

sed -i 's/\r$//' install.sh
bash install.sh

docs.title: The installer does not accept the registry access details
docs.text:
• Check that you copied the name and the token completely, without spaces.
  • The server needs internet access to the vendor's container registry.
  • If it still fails, ask your ScienceSoft representative to check that the access is active.

docs.title: aifw preflight fails
docs.text:
It says which requirement is not met. Typical causes:

Message about What to do Memory, CPU or disk Add resources. See Prerequisites. A port is in use Stop what uses it, or choose another HTTPS option. The registry cannot be reached Check the proxy and firewall rules for outgoing traffic. systemd The server must use systemd.

docs.title: Setup stops at "Start secure web access"
docs.text:
You see this message: "Start secure web access — failed". It is usually one of three things:

  1. The cloud firewall (for example a network security group) does not let ports 80 and 443 in.
  2. The DNS name does not point at this server yet.
  3. The certificate is still being issued. Wait a few minutes.

If you use your own load balancer, it must be fully ready before you run setup. For details, run:

docker logs ai-firewall-caddy

Fix the cause. If nothing about the answers has to change, run sudo aifw setup again.

docs.title: The server answers, but the sign-in page redirects to the wrong address or shows an error
docs.text:
The single sign-on service may have been set up for a different public address than the one your server uses.

Contact your ScienceSoft representative with the public address you gave to setup. [TBC: replace this with a fix in the product, or with a support procedure.]

docs.title: Computers get policy changes late
docs.text: A proxy that buffers responses, or an idle timeout that is too short, delays the streams. See Reverse proxy.

docs.title: I lost credentials.txt
docs.text: The file is meant to be deleted after you save its contents. If a value is lost, contact your ScienceSoft representative. [TBC: describe how to reset the administrator password and read the enrolment key.]

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
Send your ScienceSoft representative:

  • the output of sudo aifw status;
  • the output of sudo aifw doctor;
  • the last 200 lines of the log of the container that fails.

Do not send the settings file, credentials.txt, or any token.

docs.title: Roll out the agent to your computers
docs.text:
The agent is the small program that runs on each employee's computer. It checks requests to AI tools and applies the policy you set on the server. This part of the guide shows how to install it on many computers at once, and how to check that it joined your workspace.

Install the server first. You need its address and the device enrolment key.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
You need Where it comes from The installer AI-Firewall-<version>-x64.exe for Windows and AI-Firewall-<version>-arm64.pkg for macOS. ScienceSoft provides them. The server address The public address you gave to setup, for example https://ai-firewall.example.com. It must be https://. The device enrolment key Shown by server setup in credentials.txt. It is also in the admin portal under Settings, Enrolment. A way to deploy software Microsoft Intune, Jamf, a Group Policy startup script, or any tool that can run an installer as administrator.

[TBC: confirm where the enrolment key is shown in the admin portal in the current version.]

docs.title: Supported computers
docs.text:
System Supported Windows 10 (21H2 or newer) and Windows 11, 64-bit Intel or AMD Yes macOS on Apple silicon (M1 or newer) Yes macOS on Intel Macs No Linux No

[TBC: confirm the minimum Windows and macOS versions.]

docs.title: The enrolment key
docs.text:
The key joins a computer to your workspace. It is one key for the whole organisation. When a computer joins, it gets its own credential and stores it in the system keychain. The shared key is not used again by that computer.

  • Anyone who has the key can join a computer to your workspace. Keep it in a password manager or a secret store. Do not put it in a ticket, a chat, or a script on a shared drive that everyone can read.
  • Pass it to the installer when you deploy. After the pilot, consider replacing the key (see below).
  • If the key is wrong, the computer does not appear in the portal. It keeps working on its own, with the local default settings. Nothing is blocked, but the policy does not reach it.
  • If you replace the key on the server, installers that you already built or scripted with the old key no longer join computers. Update your deployment. For computers that are already installed, the address is read only at installation, so reinstall them to change it.

[TBC: product team to confirm key rotation and what happens to installed computers.]

docs.title: What the installer changes on a computer
docs.text:
Tell your security team about this before the pilot. AI Firewall is installed on your own managed computers, to check traffic to AI services.

On Windows:

  • Installs the app in C:\Program Files\AI Firewall. The folder is locked, so a standard user cannot change it.
  • Creates a certificate for this computer (called "AI Firewall Local CA") and adds it to the computer's trusted root certificates. The private key stays on the computer.
  • Sets a computer-wide proxy setting that sends AI traffic to the local firewall, and sets Chrome, Edge and Firefox to use it.
  • Installs protection services and scheduled tasks that restart the app. A standard user cannot stop them.
  • Needs no restart.

On macOS:

  • Installs the app in /Applications.
  • Creates a certificate for this Mac and trusts it in the System keychain.
  • Installs background services, and sets the automatic proxy setting of every network connection to the local firewall. This replaces an automatic proxy setting that your company already has.

Network: the agent talks to your server address. It also downloads its detection models and updates. [TBC: list the hosts the models are downloaded from, so network teams can allow them.]

Uninstalling removes the certificate and the settings that AI Firewall added. See Windows and macOS.

docs.title: What the employee sees
docs.text: With a silent installation, the employee sees nothing during the installation. The app starts in the tray (the Windows notification area, or the macOS menu bar), and the tray icon shows the protection state. The employee cannot stop protection or remove it. See the User Guide for what the app shows.

docs.title: Windows: install and enrol
docs.text:
install-ai-firewall.ps1

Installs the agent silently and joins the computer to your workspace. Does nothing if AI Firewall is already installed. It checks the address and the key, runs the installer, and turns the installer's result into a simple code: 0 for success, 1 for failure.

.\install-ai-firewall.ps1 `
  -InstallerPath C:\Temp\AI-Firewall-<version>-x64.exe `
  -FleetUrl https://<your-server> `
  -EnrollmentKey <enrolment-key>

Use it as a Group Policy startup script (see Windows), as an Intune script, or by hand.

docs.title: macOS: write the enrolment file
docs.text:
seed-enrollment.sh

Writes /Library/Application Support/ai-firewall/enrollment.json with the server address and the key, readable by root only. Run it before the package. See macOS.

sudo ./seed-enrollment.sh https://<your-server> <enrolment-key>

In Jamf Pro, add the script to the policy as Before, and give the address and the key as parameters 4 and 5.

docs.title: Keep the key safe
docs.text:
• A script with the key in it can join computers to your workspace. Keep it where only computer accounts or administrators can read it.
  • Do not paste the key into a ticket or a chat.
  • After the pilot, consider replacing the key.

docs.title: Not provided
docs.text: AI Firewall has no Group Policy template, no Intune configuration profile and no macOS configuration profile. Templates that you may have seen for other ScienceSoft products do not work with it.

docs.title: macOS
docs.text: AI Firewall for macOS runs on Apple silicon Macs (M1 or newer). There is no Intel version.

docs.title: The installer
docs.text:
File Use AI-Firewall-<version>-arm64.pkg Deploying to many Macs. Signed and notarized. .dmg and .zip Manual installation by one person, and automatic updates.

Use the .pkg for managed deployment. It installs for the whole Mac, never for one user only.

docs.title: The enrolment key goes in a file, not in the command
docs.text:
On macOS the installer takes no arguments. The enrolment key and the server address are read from a file that you create before you run the installer:

/Library/Application Support/ai-firewall/enrollment.json

{"fleetUrl": "https://ai-firewall.example.com", "token": "<enrolment-key>"}
  • The address must be https://. The key must be plain text without spaces.
  • The file must belong to root, group wheel, and be readable by root only (mode 0600). It holds the key.
  • The installer reads the file once, and moves the values into a protected settings file.

A script that writes this file is on the downloads page.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
From the command line, as an administrator:

sudo installer -pkg AI-Firewall-<version>-arm64.pkg -target /

The target must be /, the system volume.

docs.title: Jamf Pro
docs.text:
1. Upload the .pkg to Jamf.
  2. Upload the script that writes enrollment.json (see downloads). Give it the server address and the key as parameters.
  3. Create a policy that has both. Set the script to run Before the package.
  4. Scope the policy to a pilot smart group first.

docs.title: Other tools
docs.text: Any tool that can run a script as root and then install a .pkg works in the same way: write the file, then install.

docs.title: What the installer does
docs.text:
It runs as root and:

  • creates a certificate for this Mac and trusts it in the System keychain. If trusting fails, your MDM must deliver a trust profile, or an administrator must approve it;
  • installs the background services;
  • sets the automatic proxy configuration of every network connection to the local firewall. This replaces an automatic proxy setting that your company already has.

No special permissions (Full Disk Access and similar) need to be granted.

[TBC: confirm that no privacy permissions or system extension approvals are needed in the current version.]

AI Firewall does not provide a configuration profile (.mobileconfig). The profiles that you may find for other ScienceSoft products do not work with it.

docs.title: Remove the agent
docs.text:
Run the uninstall script that comes with the app, as root:

sudo "/Applications/AI Firewall.app/Contents/Resources/uninstall.command"

It removes the app, the services, the certificate and the proxy setting if it points at AI Firewall. When it is run as root by your management tool, it skips the steps that belong to a single user.

[TBC: confirm how the script behaves without a person at the keyboard (it asks for a confirmation when run in a terminal), and its two known issues. See the User Guide.]

When the script is run by your management tool, no notice reaches your server. The Mac stops reporting. Remove it from the portal.

docs.title: In the admin portal
docs.text:
[screenshot: admin portal: the Devices list]

Open the admin portal at https://<your-server>/admin and go to Devices. A computer that has joined appears within a few seconds. Check:

  • that it is online;
  • that it has received the policy (the policy version is shown).

If you deployed to a pilot group, compare the number of computers in the list with the number you targeted.

docs.title: On the computer
docs.text:
Windows

Check Where The enrolment file exists %PROGRAMDATA%\ai-firewall\enrollment.json The outcome of the installation %PROGRAMDATA%\ai-firewall\install-enrolment.log says whether enrolment worked, or why it was skipped. It never contains the key. The app is connected Open the app, then Device & coverage. The fleet line shows your server.

macOS

Check Where The file that you wrote /Library/Application Support/ai-firewall/enrollment.json The app is connected Open the app, then Device & coverage. The fleet line shows your server.

Also check Certificate trust. It must say Yes — installed. See the User Guide.

docs.title: If a computer does not appear
docs.text:
What you see Likely cause What to do The computer works, but is not in the portal The key or the address is missing or wrong. On Windows, one of the two switches was missing: both are needed Check install-enrolment.log. Reinstall with both values. The log says enrolment was skipped The address was not https://, or was cut off Give the full https:// address in quotes. The portal does not show it, and the app says it cannot reach the server A firewall or proxy blocks the server address Allow the address of your server from the computers. It joined once, and is now shown as offline The computer is off, or cannot reach the server Wait. Check the network. It was removed from the portal An administrator revoked it Reinstall. Computers installed before you replaced the key do not join They were installed with the old key Reinstall them with the new key.

An installation that is wrong in one computer does not stop protection on that computer. See the User Guide for the status messages the user sees.

docs.title: For security teams
docs.text: The agent asks for no inbound connections. It needs outbound access to your server address, plus the update address on your server and the download addresses for its detection models. [TBC: list the model download addresses.]

docs.title: Install on one computer
docs.text: Run the installer as an administrator. You will see a short wizard and one administrator prompt. The enrolment key and the server address are given on the command line, so the computer joins your workspace by itself.

docs.title: Silent installation
docs.text:
Run the installer from an elevated command prompt, or as the system account (as Intune and most deployment tools do):

AI-Firewall-<version>-x64.exe /S /FLEET_URL="https://<your-server>" /ENROLL_TOKEN="<enrolment-key>"
Switch Meaning /S Silent: no windows. /FLEET_URL= The address of your server. Must start with https://. /ENROLL_TOKEN= The device enrolment key. /UPDATE_URL= Optional. Where the agent looks for updates, usually https://<your-server>/updates/generic. /D=<folder> Optional. The install folder. It must be the last switch. A drive root or a system folder is refused.
  • Give both /FLEET_URL and /ENROLL_TOKEN. If only one is given, the installer ignores both and the computer works on its own, without your workspace.
  • Put the values in quotes. If you start the installer from PowerShell, use Start-Process -Wait and read the exit code.
  • The installer does not restart the computer.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning What to do 0 Installed Success. 1 Cancelled Someone stopped the wizard. 2 Failed The install folder was refused, or the previous version could not be removed. Try again, and look at the installer log. 3 Installed, with a warning The app is installed, but part of the protection could not be locked down. Review the warning in the Windows event log (source "AI Firewall").

A deployment with no server address still returns 0. Check the result with Check that computers joined.

docs.title: Microsoft Intune
docs.text:
[screenshot: Intune Win32 app: the program page with the install command]

The installer is an .exe, not an .msi. Deploy it as a Windows app (Win32).

  1. Put the .exe alone in an empty folder.
  2. Wrap it with the Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool (IntuneWinAppUtil.exe). It produces an .intunewin file.
  3. In Intune, add a Windows app (Win32) and upload the file.

  4. Set the commands:

    Setting Value Install command AI-Firewall-<version>-x64.exe /S /FLEET_URL="https://<your-server>" /ENROLL_TOKEN="<enrolment-key>" Uninstall command "%ProgramFiles%\AI Firewall\Uninstall AI Firewall.exe" /S Install behavior System Restart behavior No specific action

  5. Detection rule: a file exists, %ProgramFiles%\AI Firewall\AI Firewall.exe.

  6. Requirements: 64-bit, Windows 10 21H2 or newer.
  7. Return codes: add code 3 as Success, in addition to the defaults.
  8. Assign the app to a pilot group first.

The key is visible in Intune

The install command is stored in Intune with the key in it. Limit who can read the app's settings, and replace the key after the pilot if you are concerned.

[TBC: confirm the uninstall command and the detection rule on a pilot computer. The installer's uninstall entry in the registry can also be used for detection.]

docs.title: Group Policy (startup script)
docs.text:
AI Firewall has no Group Policy template (.admx). To use Group Policy, run the installer from a computer startup script:

  1. Put the installer on a share that computer accounts can read.
  2. Add a startup script (Computer Configuration, Policies, Windows Settings, Scripts, Startup) that runs the installer if the app is not installed yet. See Scripts to download.
  3. Link the policy to a pilot organisational unit first.

The enrolment key is on the command line of the script. Protect the share, so that only computer accounts can read it.

docs.title: Remove the agent
docs.text:
The uninstaller needs administrator rights.

"%ProgramFiles%\AI Firewall\Uninstall AI Firewall.exe" /S

It removes the app, the services, the certificate and the settings that AI Firewall added. It does not restore a computer-wide proxy setting that existed before AI Firewall was installed. Local data of every user on the computer is deleted. See the User Guide for what is removed.

When your deployment tool runs the uninstaller as the system account, no notice is sent to your server. The computer stops reporting. Remove it from the portal.
